questions.q: For $0 < a < 1$, the value of the integral ${∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{dx}{1 - 2acosx + {a}^{2}}$ is :
questions.solution:
Given: $I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{dx}{1 - 2acosx + {a}^{2}} . . . \left(i\right)$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{dx}{1 - 2acos\left(\pi - x\right) + {a}^{2}}$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{dx}{1 + 2acosx + {a}^{2}} . . . \left(ii\right)$

Adding $\left(i\right)$ and $\left(ii\right)$,

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{dx}{1 - 2acosx + {a}^{2}} + {∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{dx}{1 + 2acosx + {a}^{2}}$

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 - 2acosx + {a}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{1 + 2acosx + {a}^{2}}\right)dx$

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left(\dfrac{1 + 2acosx + {a}^{2} + 1 - 2acosx + {a}^{2}}{{\left(1 + {a}^{2}\right)}^{2} - {\left(2acosx\right)}^{2}}\right)dx$

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left(\dfrac{2\left(1 + {a}^{2}\right)}{{\left(1 + {a}^{2}\right)}^{2} - {\left(2acosx\right)}^{2}}\right)dx$

$⇒ 2I = 2{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2\left(1 + {a}^{2}\right)}{{\left(1 + {a}^{2}\right)}^{2} - 4{a}^{2}\cos^{2}x}dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2\left(1 + {a}^{2}\right) \cdot {sec}^{2}x}{{\left(1 + {a}^{2}\right)}^{2} \cdot {sec}^{2}x - 4{a}^{2}}dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2\left(1 + {a}^{2}\right) \cdot {sec}^{2}x}{{\left(1 + {a}^{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left(1 + {a}^{2}\right)}^{2}\tan^{2}x - 4{a}^{2}}dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2\left(1 + {a}^{2}\right) \cdot {sec}^{2}x}{{\left(1 + {a}^{2} - 2a\right)}^{2} + {\left(1 + {a}^{2}\right)}^{2}\tan^{2}x}dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2 \cdot \left(1 + {a}^{2}\right) \cdot {sec}^{2}x}{{\left(1 + {a}^{2}\right)}^{2} \cdot \tan^{2}x + {\left(1 - {a}^{2}\right)}^{2}}dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\dfrac{2 \cdot {sec}^{2}x}{1 + {a}^{2}} \cdot dx}{\tan^{2}x + {\left(\dfrac{1 - {a}^{2}}{1 + {a}^{2}}\right)}^{2}}$

Let, $tanx = t$

$⇒ {sec}^{2}xdx = dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{2}{1 + {a}^{2}}{∫}_{0}^{\infty}\dfrac{dt}{{t}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{1 - {a}^{2}}{1 + {a}^{2}}\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{2}{1 + {a}^{2}} \times \dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{1 - {a}^{2}}{1 + {a}^{2}}\right)}{\left[\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{t}{\left(\dfrac{1 - {a}^{2}}{1 + {a}^{2}}\right)}\right]}_{0}^{\infty}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{2}{1 - {a}^{2}}\left[\tan^{- 1}\left(\infty\right) - \tan^{- 1}\left(0\right)\right]$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{2}{\left(1 - {a}^{2}\right)}\left[\dfrac{\pi}{2} - 0\right]$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\pi}{1 - {a}^{2}}$

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}g\left(t\right){\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{1 - t}{1 + t}\right)dt$, where $g$ is a continuous odd function. If ${∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(f\left(x\right) + \dfrac{{x}^{2}cosx}{1 + {e}^{x}}\right)dx = {\left(\dfrac{\pi}{\alpha}\right)}^{2} - \alpha$, then $\alpha$ is equal to _____.
questions.solution:
Given: $f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}g\left(t\right)log\left(\dfrac{1 - t}{1 + t}\right)dt$

$⇒ f\left(- x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{- x}g\left(t\right)log\left(\dfrac{1 - t}{1 + t}\right)dt$

$⇒ f\left(- x\right) = - {∫}_{0}^{x}g\left(- y\right)log\left(\dfrac{1 + y}{1 - y}\right)dy$

$= - {∫}_{0}^{x}g ( y ) ln\left(\dfrac{1 - y}{1 + y}\right)dy$ ($g$ is odd)

$f ( - x ) = - f ( x ) ⇒ f$ is also odd.

Now,

$I = {∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(f ( x ) + \dfrac{{x}^{2}cosx}{1 + {e}^{x}}\right)dx . . . \left(i\right)$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(f ( - x ) + \dfrac{{x}^{2}{e}^{x}cosx}{1 + {e}^{x}}\right)dx . . . \left(ii\right)$

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}{x}^{2}cosxdx$

$⇒ 2I = 2{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}{x}^{2}cosxdx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}{x}^{2}cosxdx$

$⇒ I = {\left({x}^{2}sinx\right)}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}} - {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}2xsinxdx$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{4} - 2{\left(- xcosx + sinx\right)}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{4} - 2 ( 0 + 1 )$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{4} - 2$

$⇒ I = {\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{2} - 2$

$∴ \alpha = 2$

questions.q: If $( a, b )$ be the orthocentre of the triangle whose vertices are $( 1, 2 ) , ( 2, 3 )$ and $( 3, 1 )$, and ${I}_{1} = {∫}_{a}^{b}xsin\left(4x - {x}^{2}\right)dx, {I}_{2} = {∫}_{a}^{b}sin\left(4x - {x}^{2}\right)dx$ , then $36\dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}}$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Equation of $CE$ is given by,

$⇒ \left(y - 1\right) = \dfrac{- 1}{\dfrac{3 - 2}{2 - 1}}\left(x - 3\right)$

$⇒ \left(y - 1\right) = - ( x - 3 )$

$⇒ x + y = 4 . . . \left(i\right)$

Similarly, equation of $AD$ is given by,

$⇒ \left(y - 2\right) = \dfrac{- 1}{\dfrac{3 - 1}{2 - 3}}\left(x - 1\right)$

$⇒ \left(y - 2\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(x - 1\right)$

$⇒ 2y - 4 = x - 1$

$⇒ x - 2y + 3 = 0$

Using $\left(i\right)$

$⇒ 4 - y - 2y + 3 = 0$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{7}{3}$

$⇒ x = 4 - \dfrac{7}{3}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{5}{3}$

So, Orthocentre is $H ≡ \left(a, b\right) = \left(\dfrac{5}{3}, \dfrac{7}{3}\right)$.

Orthocentre lies on the line $x + y = 4$

So, $a + b = 4$

Now, ${I}_{1} = {∫}_{a}^{b}xsin ( x ( 4 - x ) ) dx . . . ( 1 )$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {∫}_{a}^{b} ( a + b - x ) sin ( \left(a + b - x\right) ( 4 - \left(a + b - x\right) ) ) dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {∫}_{a}^{b} ( 4 - x ) sin ( x ( 4 - x ) ) dx . . . ( 2 )$

Using, $( 1 ) + ( 2 )$

$⇒ 2{I}_{1} = {∫}_{a}^{b}4sin ( x ( 4 - x ) ) dx$

$⇒ 2{I}_{1} = 4{I}_{2}$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = 2{I}_{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} = 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{36{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} = 72$

questions.q: If ${∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{\left(5 + 2x - 2{x}^{2}\right)\left(1 + {e}^{\left(2 - 4x\right)}\right)}dx = \dfrac{1}{\alpha}{\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{\alpha + 1}{\beta}\right), \alpha, \beta > 0$, then ${\alpha}^{4} - {\beta}^{4}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

${∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{\left(5 + 2x - 2{x}^{2}\right)\left(1 + {e}^{\left(2 - 4x\right)}\right)}dx = \dfrac{1}{\alpha}{\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{\alpha + 1}{\beta}\right)$

Now let,

$I = \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{5}{2} - \left({x}^{2} - x\right)\right)\left(1 + {e}^{- 4\left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)}\right)}dx$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{\left(\left(\dfrac{11}{4}\right) - {\left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{2}\right)\left(1 + {e}^{- 4\left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)}\right)}dx$

Now let $x - \dfrac{1}{2} = t ⇒ dx = dt$

So, integral becomes,

$I = \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{\dfrac{- 1}{2}}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}\dfrac{1}{\left{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{2}\right)}^{2} - {t}^{2}\right)\left(1 + {e}^{- 4t}\right)}dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{\dfrac{- 1}{2}}^{0}\dfrac{1}{\left{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{2}\right)}^{2} - {t}^{2}\right)\left(1 + {e}^{- 4t}\right)}dt + \mathop{\mathop{\dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}\dfrac{1}{\left{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{2}\right)}^{2} - {t}^{2}\right)\left(1 + {e}^{- 4t}\right)}dt}_{⏟}}_{{I}_{2}}$

Now solving ${I}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{\dfrac{- 1}{2}}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}\dfrac{1}{\left{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{2}\right)}^{2} - {t}^{2}\right)\left(1 + {e}^{- 4t}\right)}dt$,

Let $t = - z$, we get $dt = - dz$

So, ${I}_{2} = - \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}^{0}\dfrac{dz}{\left{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{2}\right)}^{2} - {z}^{2}\right)\left(1 + {e}^{4z}\right)}$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}\dfrac{dt}{\left{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{2}\right)}^{2} - {t}^{2}\right)\left(1 + {e}^{4t}\right)}$

Now putting the value of ${I}_{2}\text{in}I$ we get,

$I = \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}\dfrac{1}{\left({\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{2}\right)}^{2} - {t}^{2}\right)\left(1 + {e}^{- 4t}\right)} + \dfrac{1}{\left({\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{2}\right)}^{2} - {t}^{2}\right)\left(1 + {e}^{4t}\right)}dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}\dfrac{{e}^{4t}}{\left({\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{2}\right)}^{2} - {t}^{2}\right)\left({e}^{4t} + 1\right)} + \dfrac{1}{\left({\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{2}\right)}^{2} - {t}^{2}\right)\left(1 + {e}^{4t}\right)}dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}\dfrac{1}{{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{2}\right)}^{2} - {t}^{2}}dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{2}\right)}{\left[ln\left|\dfrac{\dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{2} + t}{\dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{2} - t}\right|\right]}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{11}}ln\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{11} + 1}{\sqrt{11} - 1}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{11}}ln\left(\dfrac{( \sqrt{11} + 1{)}^{2}}{10}\right)$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{11}}ln\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{11} + 1}{\sqrt{10}}\right)$

Now on comparing with $\dfrac{1}{\alpha}{\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{\alpha + 1}{\beta}\right)$ we get,

$⇒ \alpha = \sqrt{11}, \beta = \sqrt{10} ⇒ {\alpha}^{4} - {\beta}^{4} = 21$

questions.q: Let ${f}_{n} = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}\sin^{k - 1}x\right)\left(\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n} ( 2k - 1 ) \sin^{k - 1}x\right)cosxdx, n \in \mathbb{N} .$ Then ${f}_{21} - {f}_{20}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

${f}_{n} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\left(\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}\sin^{k - 1}x\right)\left(\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n} ( 2k - 1 ) \sin^{k - 1}x\right)cosxdx$

Now let, $sinx = t$

$⇒ cosxdx = dt$

So, ${f}_{n} = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n} ( t{)}^{k - 1}\right)\left(\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n} ( 2k - 1 ) ( t{)}^{k - 1}\right)dt$

$⇒ {f}_{n} = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(1 + t + {t}^{2} . . . . + {t}^{n - 1}\right)\left(1 + 3t + 5{t}^{2} + . . . . . + \left(2n - 1\right){t}^{n - 1}\right)dt$

Now multiply and divide by $\sqrt{t}$ we get,

$⇒ {f}_{n} = {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{\left({t}^{\dfrac{1}{2}} + {t}^{\dfrac{3}{2}} + t\dfrac{5}{2} . . . . + {t}^{\dfrac{2n - 1}{2}}\right)}{\sqrt{t}}\left(1 + 3t + 5{t}^{2} + . . . . . + \left(2n - 1\right){t}^{n - 1}\right)dt$

$⇒ {f}_{n} = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(t\dfrac{1}{2} + t\dfrac{3}{2} + t\dfrac{5}{2} . . . . + t\dfrac{2n - 1}{2}\right)\left(t\dfrac{- 1}{2} + 3t\dfrac{1}{2} + 5t\dfrac{3}{2} + . . . . . + \left(2n - 1\right)t\dfrac{2n - 3}{2}\right)dt$

Now let $t\dfrac{1}{2} + t\dfrac{3}{2} + t\dfrac{5}{2} . . . . + t\dfrac{2n - 1}{2} = z$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}\left(t\dfrac{- 1}{2} + 3t\dfrac{1}{2} + 5t\dfrac{3}{2} + . . . . . + \left(2n - 1\right)t\dfrac{2n - 3}{2}\right)dt = dz$

Hence, the integral becomes,

$⇒ {f}_{n} = 2{∫}_{0}^{n}zdz$

$⇒ {f}_{n} = {\left[{z}^{2}\right]}_{0}^{n} = {n}^{2}$

Hence, ${f}_{21} - {f}_{20} = {21}^{2} - {20}^{2} = 41$

questions.q:
Among

$\left(S1\right): \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}} ( 2 + 4 + 6 + \ldots + 2n ) = 1$

$\left(S2\right): \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{1}{{n}^{16}}\left({1}^{15} + {2}^{15} + {3}^{15} + \ldots + {n}^{15}\right) = \dfrac{1}{16}$
questions.solution:
${S}_{1}: \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}} [ 2 + 4 + 6 + \ldots + 2n ]$

$\lim_{n \to \infty}2\dfrac{n ( n + 1 )}{2{n}^{2}} = 1$

${S}_{2}: \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{1}{{n}^{16}}\left({1}^{15} + {2}^{15} + {3}^{15} + \ldots + {n}^{15}\right)$

This is limit of sum.

We know that $\lim_{n \to \infty}\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}f\left(\dfrac{r}{n}\right)\dfrac{1}{n} = {∫}_{0}^{1}f\left(x\right) d x$

$∵ \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}{r}^{k}}{{n}^{k + 1}} = \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}{\left(\dfrac{r}{n}\right)}^{k}}{n}$

$= {∫}_{0}^{1}{x}^{k} d x = \dfrac{1}{k + 1}$

Here $k = 15$

$∴ \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}{r}^{15}}{{n}^{16}} = \dfrac{1}{16}$

$∴$ Both $S1$ and $S2$ are correct

Hence this is the required option.

questions.q: Let for $x \in \mathbb{R}, {S}_{0}\left(x\right) = x, {S}_{k}\left(x\right) = {C}_{k}x + k{∫}_{0}^{x}{S}_{k - 1}\left(t\right)dt$ where ${C}_{0} = 1, {C}_{k} = 1 - {∫}_{0}^{1}{S}_{k - 1}\left(x\right)dx, k = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$ Then ${S}_{2}\left(3\right) + 6{C}_{3}$ is equal to $_______ .$
questions.solution:
Given,

${S}_{0}\left(x\right) = x, {S}_{k}\left(x\right) = {C}_{k}x + k{∫}_{0}^{x}{S}_{k - 1}\left(t\right)dt$

Now for ${S}_{0}\left(x\right) = x, {C}_{0} = 1$

Now solving, ${C}_{k} = 1 - {∫}_{0}^{1}{S}_{k - 1}\left(x\right)dx$ for $k = 1$ we get,

${C}_{1} = 1 - {∫}_{0}^{1}xdx = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Now putting $k = 1$ in ${S}_{k}\left(x\right) = {C}_{k}x + k{∫}_{0}^{x}{S}_{k - 1}\left(t\right)dt$ we get,

$⇒ {S}_{1}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x}{2} + 1 \cdot {∫}_{0}^{x}tdt = \dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}$

Now for $k = 2$ we get,

${C}_{2} = 1 - {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right)dx = \dfrac{7}{12}$

And ${S}_{2}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{7}{12}x + 2{∫}_{0}^{x}\left(\dfrac{t}{2} + \dfrac{{t}^{2}}{2}\right)dt$

$⇒ {S}_{2}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{7x}{12} + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3}$

Now taking $k = 3$ we get,

${C}_{3} = 1 - {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\dfrac{7x}{12} + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3}\right)dx = \dfrac{11}{24}$

Now finding the value of${S}_{2}\left(3\right) + 6 \cdot {C}_{3}$ we get,

${S}_{2}\left(3\right) + 6 \cdot {C}_{3} = \dfrac{7 \times 3}{12} + \dfrac{{3}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{3}^{3}}{3} + 6 \times \dfrac{11}{24}$

$⇒ {S}_{2}\left(3\right) + 6 \cdot {C}_{3} = \dfrac{61}{4} + \dfrac{11}{4} = 18$

${C}_{1} = 1 - {∫}_{0}^{1}xdx = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Now putting $k = 1$ in ${S}_{k}\left(x\right) = {C}_{k}x + k{∫}_{0}^{x}{S}_{k - 1}\left(t\right)dt$ we get,

$⇒ {S}_{1}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x}{2} + 1 \cdot {∫}_{0}^{x}tdt = \dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}$

Now for $k = 2$ we get,

${C}_{2} = 1 - {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right)dx = \dfrac{7}{12}$

And ${S}_{2}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{7}{12}x + 2{∫}_{0}^{x}\left(\dfrac{t}{2} + \dfrac{{t}^{2}}{2}\right)dt$

$⇒ {S}_{2}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{7x}{12} + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3}$

Now taking $k = 3$ we get,

${C}_{3} = 1 - {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\dfrac{7x}{12} + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3}\right)dx = \dfrac{11}{24}$

Now finding the value of${S}_{2}\left(3\right) + 6 \cdot {C}_{3}$ we get,

${S}_{2}\left(3\right) + 6 \cdot {C}_{3} = \dfrac{7 \times 3}{12} + \dfrac{{3}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{3}^{3}}{3} + 6 \times \dfrac{11}{24}$

$⇒ {S}_{2}\left(3\right) + 6 \cdot {C}_{3} = \dfrac{61}{4} + \dfrac{11}{4} = 18$

Then the value of the integral ${∫}_{0}^{2}xf\left(x\right)dx$ is
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}{e}^{min\left\{{x}^{2}, x - \left[x\right]\right\}}, & x \in [ 0, 1 ) \\ {e}^{\left[x - {\log}_{e}x\right]}, & x \in \left[1, 2\right]\end{cases}\right$
$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}{e}^{{x}^{2}} & x \in [ 0, 1 ) \\ e, & x \in \left[1, 2\right]\end{cases}\right$

As $x - lnx \in [ 1, 2 )$ for $x \in [ 1, 2 ]$, so$\left[x - lnx\right] = 1$ and $x - \left[x\right] = \left\{x\right\}$, so $x \in \left(0, 1\right), {x}^{2} < \left\{x\right\}$

Now solving the integral we get,${∫}_{0}^{2}xf\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{1}x \cdot {e}^{{x}^{2}}dx + {∫}_{1}^{2}x \cdot edx$

Now in first integral, let ${x}^{2} = t ⇒ 2xdx = dt$ we get,

$⇒ {∫}_{0}^{2}xf\left(x\right) = \left[\dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}{e}^{t}dt\right] + {\left[e \cdot \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right]}_{1}^{2}$

$⇒ {∫}_{0}^{2}xf\left(x\right) = \left(\dfrac{e - 1}{2}\right) + \dfrac{3e}{2}$

$⇒ {∫}_{0}^{2}xf\left(x\right) = 2e - \dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.q: If $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a continuous function satisfying ${∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}f\left(sin2x\right)sinxdx + \alpha{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}f\left(cos2x\right)cosxdx = 0$, then the value of $\alpha$ is
questions.solution:
Given,

${∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}f\left(sin2x\right)sinxdx + \alpha{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}f\left(cos2x\right)cosxdx = 0$

Now, let $I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}f\left(sin2x\right) . sinxdx$

Now using property ${∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right) d x = {∫}_{a}^{c}f\left(x\right) d x + {∫}_{c}^{b}f\left(x\right) d x$ we get,
$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}f\left(sin2x\right)sinxdx + {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}f\left(sin2x\right) . sinxdx$

Now using property ${∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right) d x = {∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right) d x$ we get,

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}f\left(cos2x\right)sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - x\right)dx + {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}f\left(sin2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + x\right)\right)sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + x\right)dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}f\left(cos2x\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}cosx - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}sinx\right)dx + {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}f\left(cos2x\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}cosx + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}sinx\right)dx$
$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}f\left(cos2x\right)\left(\sqrt{2}cosx\right)dx$

So, the putting the value of $I$ in ${∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}f\left(sin2x\right)sinxdx + \alpha{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}f\left(cos2x\right)cosxdx = 0$ we get, $\alpha = - \sqrt{2}$

questions.q: The value of the integral ${∫}_{- {\log}_{e}2}^{{\log}_{e}2}{e}^{x}\left({\log}_{e}\left({e}^{x} + \sqrt{1 + {e}^{2x}}\right)\right)dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $I = {∫}_{- {\log}_{e}2}^{{\log}_{e}2}{e}^{x}\left[{\log}_{e}\left({e}^{x} + \sqrt{1 + {e}^{2x}}\right)\right]dx$

Let us substitute ${e}^{x} = t$

$⇒ {e}^{x}dx = dt$

Lower limit $= {e}^{- {\log}_{e}\left(2\right)} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Upper limit $= {e}^{{\log}_{e}\left(2\right)} = 2$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}^{2}1 \times {\log}_{e}\left[t + \sqrt{1 + {t}^{2}}\right]dt$

Apply integration by-parts.

$∫ u\left(t\right)v\left(t\right)dt = u\left(t\right) ∫ v\left(t\right)dt - ∫ \left(u ' \left(t\right) ∫ v\left(t\right)dt\right)dt$

Take $u\left(t\right) = {\log}_{e}\left[t + \sqrt{1 + {t}^{2}}\right], v\left(t\right) = 1$

$⇒ u ' \left(t\right) = \dfrac{1}{t + \sqrt{1 + {t}^{2}}}\left(1 + \dfrac{2t}{2\sqrt{1 + {t}^{2}}}\right) = t$

$= {\left[tln\left(\sqrt{{t}^{2} + 1} + x\right)\right]}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}^{2} - {∫}_{1 / 2}^{2}\dfrac{t}{\sqrt{{t}^{2} + 1}}dt$

$= {\left[tln\sqrt{{t}^{2} + 1} + t - \sqrt{{t}^{2} + 1}\right]}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}^{2}$

$= \left[2ln\left(\sqrt{5} + 2\right) - \sqrt{5}\right] - \left[\dfrac{1}{2}ln\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) - \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}}\right]$

$= ln\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2} ( 2 + \sqrt{5}{)}^{2}}{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{5}}}\right) - \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{2}$

Hence this is the correct option.

questions.q: For $m, n > 0$, let $\alpha\left(m, n\right) = {∫}_{0}^{2}{t}^{m}{\left(1 + 3t\right)}^{n}dt$. If ,$11\alpha\left(10, 6\right) + 18\alpha\left(11, 5\right) = p{\left(14\right)}^{6}$, then $p$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$\alpha\left(m, n\right) = {∫}_{0}^{2}{t}^{m}{\left(1 + 3t\right)}^{n}dt$

Now using integration by parts we get,

$⇒ \alpha\left(m, n\right) = {\left{\left(1 + 3t\right)}^{n} ⋅ \dfrac{{t}^{m + 1}}{m + 1}\right|}_{0}^{2} - {∫}_{0}^{2}n{\left(1 + 3t\right)}^{n - 1} \times 3 ⋅ \dfrac{{t}^{m + 1}}{m + 1}dt$

$⇒ \left(m + 1\right)\alpha\left(m, n\right) = {\left{\left(1 + 3t\right)}^{n} ⋅ \left({t}^{m + 1}\right)\right|}_{0}^{2} - 3n\left(m + 1\right){∫}_{0}^{2}{\left(1 + 3t\right)}^{n - 1} \times {t}^{m + 1}dt$

$⇒ \left(m + 1\right)\alpha\left(m, n\right) = {\left(1 + 3 \times 2\right)}^{n} ⋅ \left({2}^{m + 1}\right) - 3n\left(m + 1\right)\alpha\left(m + 1, n - 1\right)$

$⇒ \left(m + 1\right)\alpha\left(m, n\right) = {7}^{n} \cdot {2}^{m + 1} - 3n\alpha\left(m + 1, n - 1\right)$

$⇒ \left(m + 1\right)\alpha\left(m, n\right) + 3n\alpha\left(m + 1, n - 1\right) = {7}^{n} \cdot {2}^{m + 1}$

Now put $m = 10, n = 6$ in above equation we get,

$11\alpha\left(10, 6\right) + 18\alpha\left(11, 5\right) = {7}^{6} \cdot {2}^{11} = 32 \times {\left(14\right)}^{6}$

Hence, on comparing with $11\alpha\left(10, 6\right) + 18\alpha\left(11, 5\right) = p \times {\left(14\right)}^{6}$ we get,

$⇒ p = 32$

questions.q: Let f be a continuous function satisfying ${∫}_{0}^{{t}^{2}}\left(f ( x ) + {x}^{2}\right)dx = \dfrac{4}{3}{t}^{3}, ∀ t > 0$ . Then $f\left(\dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{4}\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given equation is ${∫}_{0}^{{t}^{2}}\left(f ( x ) + {x}^{2}\right)dx = \dfrac{4}{3}{t}^{3}, ∀ t > 0$

According to Newton Leibnitz theorem we have$\dfrac{d}{d x}\left({∫}_{u\left(x\right)}^{v\left(x\right)}f\left(t\right) d t\right) = f\left(v\left(x\right)\right) \times v ' \left(x\right) - f\left(u\left(x\right)\right) \times u ' \left(x\right)$

Apply Newtons Leibnitz theorem in the given equation.

$⇒ \left(f\left({t}^{2}\right) + {t}^{4}\right)2t - 0 = 4{t}^{2}$

$⇒ f\left({t}^{2}\right) + {t}^{4} = 2t$

$⇒ f\left({x}^{2}\right) = - {x}^{4} + 2x$

$⇒ f ( x ) = - {x}^{2} + 2\sqrt{x}$

$⇒ f\left(\dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{4}\right) = - \dfrac{{\pi}^{4}}{{4}^{2}} + 2 \times \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$= \dfrac{- {\pi}^{4}}{16} + \pi$

$= \pi\left(1 - \dfrac{{\pi}^{3}}{16}\right)$

Hence this is the correct option.

Let $[ t ]$ denote the greatest integer function. If
${∫}_{0}^{2 . 4}\left[{x}^{2}\right]dx = \alpha + \beta\sqrt{2} + \gamma\sqrt{3} + \delta\sqrt{5}\text{, then}\alpha + \beta + \gamma + \delta$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given that ${∫}_{0}^{2 . 4}\left[{x}^{2}\right]dx = \alpha + \beta\sqrt{2} + \gamma\sqrt{3} + \delta\sqrt{5}\text{, then}\alpha + \beta + \gamma + \delta$

We know that for $1 \le x < 2$​, $\left[x\right] = 1$​​​​​​$⇒ {∫}_{0}^{2 . 4}\left[{x}^{2}\right]dx = {∫}_{0}^{1}0dx + {∫}_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}1dx + {∫}_{\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{3}}2dx + {∫}_{\sqrt{3}}^{2}3dx + {∫}_{2}^{\sqrt{5}}4dx + {∫}_{\sqrt{5}}^{2 . 4}5dx$

$= 0 + ( \sqrt{2} - 1 ) + 2 ( \sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2} ) + 3 ( 2 - \sqrt{3} ) + 4 ( \sqrt{5} - 2 ) + 5\left(2 . 4 - \sqrt{5}\right)$

$= 9 - \sqrt{2} - \sqrt{3} - \sqrt{5}$

This is in the form of $\alpha + \beta\sqrt{2} + \gamma\sqrt{3} + \delta\sqrt{5}$

$\alpha = 9, \beta = - 1, \gamma = - 1, \delta = - 1$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta + \gamma + \delta = 9 - 1 - 1 - 1 = 6$

Hence this is the required answer.

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right)$ be a function satisfying $f\left(x\right) + f\left(\pi - x\right) = {\pi}^{2}, ∀ x \in \mathbb{R}$. Then ${∫}_{0}^{\pi}f\left(x\right)sinxdx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let

$I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}f\left(x\right)sinxdx . . . \left(1\right)$

Now using the property ${∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right)dx$ we get,

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}f\left(\pi - x\right)sin\left(\pi - x\right)dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}f\left(\pi - x\right)sinxdx . . . \left(2\right)$

Adding $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$, we get

$2I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left[f\left(x\right) + f\left(\pi - x\right)\right]sinxdx$

$⇒ 2I = {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{\pi}sinxdx$ {as given $f\left(x\right) + f\left(\pi - x\right) = {\pi}^{2}$}

$⇒ 2I = {\pi}^{2}{\left[- cosx\right]}_{0}^{\pi}$

$⇒ 2I = 2{\pi}^{2}$

$⇒ I = {\pi}^{2}$

Hence this is the correct option.

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x}{{\left(1 + {x}^{n}\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{n}}}, x \in \mathbb{R} - \left\{- 1\right\}, n \in \mathbb{N}, n > 2$. If ${f}^{n}\left(x\right) = ( fofof . . . .$ upto $n$ times) $\left(x\right)$, then $\lim_{n \to \infty}{∫}_{0}^{1}{x}^{n - 2}\left({f}^{n}\left(x\right)\right)dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x}{{\left(1 + {x}^{n}\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{n}}}, x \in \mathbb{R} - \left\{- 1\right\}, n \in \mathbb{N}, n > 2$,

${f}^{n}\left(x\right) = ( fofof . . . .$ upto $n$ times) $\left(x\right)$,

Now finding $f\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = \dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{{\left[1 + {\left(f\left(x\right)\right)}^{n}\right]}^{\dfrac{1}{n}}}$

$⇒ f\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = \dfrac{\dfrac{x}{{\left(1 + {x}^{n}\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{n}}}}{{\left[1 + {\left(\dfrac{x}{{\left(1 + {x}^{n}\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{n}}}\right)}^{n}\right]}^{\dfrac{1}{n}}}$

$⇒ f\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = \dfrac{x}{{\left[1 + 2{x}^{n}\right]}^{\dfrac{1}{n}}}$

Similarly, ${f}^{n}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x}{{\left(1 + n{x}^{n}\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{n}}}$

Now solving the integral we get,

$I = {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{{x}^{n - 1}}{{\left(1 + n{x}^{n}\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{n}}}dx$

Now let, $1 + n{x}^{n} = {t}^{n}$

$⇒ {n}^{2}{x}^{n - 1}dx = n{t}^{n - 1}dt$

$I = {∫}_{1}^{\left(1 + n\right)\dfrac{1}{n}}\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{n}{t}^{n - 1}dt}{t}$

$⇒ I = {\left[\dfrac{1}{n}\dfrac{{t}^{n - 1}}{n - 1}\right]}_{1}^{\left(1 + n\right)\dfrac{1}{n}}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{n\left(n - 1\right)}\left({\left(1 + n\right)}^{1 - \dfrac{1}{n}} - 1\right)$

Now solving the limit we get,

$\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{{\left(1 + n\right)}^{1 - \dfrac{1}{n}} - 1}{n\left(n - 1\right)}$

Now let $n = \dfrac{1}{h}$ so the limit changes to,

$\lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{{\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{h}\right)}^{1 - h} - 1}{\dfrac{1}{h}\left(\dfrac{1}{h} - 1\right)}$

$= \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{h}\left(1 - h\right)\right) - 1}{\dfrac{1}{h}\left(\dfrac{1}{h} - 1\right)}$

$= \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{\left(1 - h\right)}{\left(\dfrac{1}{h} - 1\right)}$

$= \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{h\left(1 - h\right)}{\left(1 - h\right)}$

$= \lim_{h \to 0}h = 0$

questions.q: The value of the integral ${∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{x + \dfrac{\pi}{4}}{2 - cos2x}dx$ is :
questions.solution:
Let,

$I = {∫}_{\dfrac{- \pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{x + \dfrac{\pi}{4}}{2 - cos2x}dx \ldots \left(1\right)$

Now replacing $x \to - x$ we get,

$⇒ I = {∫}_{\dfrac{- \pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{- x + \dfrac{\pi}{4}}{2 - cos2x}dx \ldots \left(2\right)$

Now both the equation we get,

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{\dfrac{- \pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}{2 - cos2x}dx$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\pi}{4} \cdot 2{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{dx}{2 - cos2x}dx\left\{\text{as}cos2x\text{is even function}\right\}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\pi}{4} \cdot 2{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{\left(1 + \tan^{2}x\right)dx}{2\left(1 + \tan^{2}x\right) - \left(1 - \tan^{2}x\right)}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\pi}{4} \cdot 2{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{{sec}^{2}xdx}{3\tan^{2}x + 1}$

Now let $tanx = t ⇒ {sec}^{2}xdx = dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\pi}{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{dt}{3{t}^{2} + 1}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\pi}{2\sqrt{3}}\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{3}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{6\sqrt{3}}$

questions.q: If ${∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{{5}^{cosx}\left(1 + cosxcos3x + \cos^{2}x + \cos^{3}xcos3x\right)dx}{1 + {5}^{cosx}} = \dfrac{k\pi}{16}$, then $k$ is equal to _____ .
questions.solution:
Given,

$I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{{5}^{cosx}\left(1 + cosxcos3x + \cos^{2}x + \cos^{3}xcos3x\right)}{1 + {5}^{cosx}}dx . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now using the property ${∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right) d x = {∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right) d x$ we get,

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{{5}^{- cosx}\left(1 + cosxcos3x + \cos^{2}x + \cos^{3}xcos3x\right)}{1 + {5}^{- cosx}}dx . . . . \left(2\right)$

Now adding above equations we get,

$2I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left(1 + cosxcos3x + \cos^{2}x + \cos^{3}xcos3x\right)dx$

Now using the property ${∫}_{0}^{2a}f\left(x\right) d x = 2{∫}_{a}^{a}f\left(x\right) d x\left\{\text{when}f\left(x\right)\text{is even}\right\}$

$⇒ 2I = 2{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(1 + cosxcos3x + \cos^{2}x + \cos^{3}xcos3x\right)dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(1 + cosxcos3x + \cos^{2}x + \cos^{3}xcos3x\right)dx . . . . . \left(3\right)$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(1 + sinx\left(- sin3x\right) + \sin^{2}x - \sin^{3}xsin3x\right)dx . . . . \left(4\right)$

Now adding equation $\left(3\right) \text{ and } \left(4\right)$ we get,

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(3 + cos4x + \cos^{3}xcos3x - \sin^{3}xsin3x\right)dx$

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}3 + cos4x + \left(\dfrac{cos3x + 3cosx}{4}\right)cos3x - sin3x\left(\dfrac{3sinx - sin3x}{4}\right)dx$

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(3 + cos4x + \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4}cos4x\right)dx$

$⇒ 2I = \dfrac{13}{4} \times \dfrac{\pi}{2} + \dfrac{7}{4}{\left(\dfrac{sin4x}{4}\right)}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{13\pi}{16}$,

Now on comparing with $\dfrac{k\pi}{16}$, we get $k = 13$

questions.q: $\lim_{n \to \infty}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + n} + \dfrac{1}{2 + n} + \dfrac{1}{3 + n} + \ldots + \dfrac{1}{2n}\right)$ is equal to :-
questions.solution:
We have,

$\lim_{n \to \infty}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + n} + \dfrac{1}{2 + n} + \dfrac{1}{3 + n} + \ldots + \dfrac{1}{2n}\right)$

$= \lim_{n \to \infty}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + n} + \dfrac{2}{1 + n} + \dfrac{3}{1 + n} + \ldots . + \dfrac{1}{n + n}\right)$

$= \lim_{n \to \infty}\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}\dfrac{1}{n + r}$

$= \lim_{n \to \infty}\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}\dfrac{1}{n}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + \dfrac{r}{n}}\right)$

$= {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{1 + x}dx$

$= {\left[{\log}_{e}\left(1 + x\right)\right]}_{0}^{1}$

$= {\log}_{e}\left(2\right)$

questions.q: Let $\alpha > 0$. If ${∫}_{0}^{\alpha}\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x + \alpha} - \sqrt{x}}dx = \dfrac{16 + 20\sqrt{2}}{15}$ then $\alpha$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Given,

${∫}_{0}^{\alpha}\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x + \alpha} - \sqrt{x}}dx = \dfrac{16 + 20\sqrt{2}}{15} . . . . ( 1 )$

Rationalise the denominator in L.H.S we get,

${∫}_{0}^{\alpha}\dfrac{x ( \sqrt{\alpha + x} + \sqrt{x} )}{\alpha}dx = \dfrac{1}{\alpha}\left[{∫}_{0}^{\alpha}x\sqrt{\alpha + x}dx + {∫}_{0}^{\alpha}{x}^{3 / 2}dx\right]$

Put $\alpha + x = {t}^{2} ⇒ dx = 2tdt$

questions.q: Let $\alpha \in \left(0, 1\right)$ and $\beta = {\log}_{e}\left(1 - \alpha\right)$. Let ${P}_{n}\left(x\right) = x + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3} + \ldots . + \dfrac{{x}^{n}}{n}, x \in \left(0, 1\right)$. Then the integral ${∫}_{0}^{\alpha}\dfrac{{t}^{50}}{1 - t}dt$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let

$I = {∫}_{0}^{\alpha}\dfrac{{t}^{50}}{1 - t}dt$

$⇒ I = - {∫}_{0}^{\alpha}\left(\dfrac{1 - {t}^{50} - 1}{1 - t}\right)dt$

$⇒ I = - {∫}_{0}^{\alpha}\left(\dfrac{1 - {t}^{50}}{1 - t}\right)dt + {∫}_{0}^{\alpha}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 - t}\right)dt$

$⇒ I = - {∫}_{0}^{\alpha}\left(1 + t + {t}^{2} + . . . + {t}^{49}\right)dt - {\left[ln\left(1 - t\right)\right]}_{0}^{\alpha}$

$⇒ I = - {\left[t + \dfrac{{t}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{t}^{3}}{3} + . . . + \dfrac{{t}^{50}}{50}\right]}_{0}^{\alpha} - ln\left(1 - \alpha\right)$

$⇒ I = - \left[\alpha + \dfrac{{\alpha}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{\alpha}^{3}}{3} + . . . + \dfrac{{\alpha}^{50}}{50}\right] - ln\left(1 - \alpha\right)$

$⇒ I = - \left(\beta + {P}_{50}\left(\alpha\right)\right)$

questions.q: The value of ${∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\left(2 + 3sinx\right)}{sinx\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let, $I = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2 + 3sinx}{sinx\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx$

Now rearranging the above integral we get,

$I = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2}{sinx\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{3}{\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2sinx}{\sin^{2}x\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{3}{\left(2\cos^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}dx$

$⇒ I = \mathop{\mathop{{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2sinx}{\sin^{2}x\left(1 + cosx\right)} d x}_{⏟}}_{{I}_{1}} + \dfrac{3}{2}\mathop{\mathop{{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}{sec}^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) d x}_{⏟}}_{{I}_{2}}$

$⇒ I = \mathop{\mathop{{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2sinx}{\sin^{2}x\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx}_{⏟}}_{{I}_{1}} + \dfrac{3}{2} \times 2\mathop{\mathop{{\left[tan\dfrac{x}{2}\right]}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}}_{⏟}}_{{I}_{2}}$

$⇒ I = \mathop{\mathop{{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2sinx}{\sin^{2}x\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx}_{⏟}}_{{I}_{1}} + 3\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$

Now solving ${I}_{1}$ we get,

${I}_{1} = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2sinx}{\sin^{2}x\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = 2{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{1}{sinx\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = 2{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{2tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{1 + \tan^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}\right)\left(1 + \dfrac{1 - tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{1 + \tan^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}\right)}dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\left[1 + \tan^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right]{sec}^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}dx$

Put $tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) = v ⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}{sec}^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)dx = dv$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}^{1}\dfrac{\left(1 + {v}^{2}\right)dv}{v}$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {\left[{\log}_{e}\left(v\right) + \dfrac{{v}^{2}}{2}\right]}_{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}^{1}$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {\log}_{e}\left(1\right) - {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + \dfrac{1}{3}$

So,

$I = \dfrac{1}{3} + {\log}_{e}\sqrt{3} + 3\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{10}{3} - \sqrt{3} + {\log}_{e}\sqrt{3}$

questions.q: Let a differentiable function $f$ satisfy $f\left(x\right) + {∫}_{3}^{x}\dfrac{f\left(t\right)}{t}dt = \sqrt{x + 1}, x \ge 3$. Then $12f\left(8\right)$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

$f\left(x\right) + {∫}_{3}^{x}\dfrac{f\left(t\right)}{t}dt = \sqrt{x + 1}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) + \dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{x} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x + 1}}$

Put $y = f\left(x\right)$, then

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{x} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x + 1}}$

So, $I . F . = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}} = {e}^{ln\left|x\right|} = x$

Hence, solution is

$xy = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x + 1}}dx$

$⇒ xy = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \left(\dfrac{x + 1 - 1}{\sqrt{x + 1}}\right)dx$

$⇒ xy = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \left(\sqrt{x + 1} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x + 1}}\right)dx$

$⇒ xy = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\left(x + 1\right)\dfrac{3}{2} - 2\sqrt{x + 1}\right) + C$

$⇒ xy = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(x + 1\right)\dfrac{3}{2} - \sqrt{x + 1} + C$

Put $x = 3$, then $f\left(3\right) = 2$

So,

$6 = \dfrac{8}{3} - 2 + C ⇒ C = \dfrac{16}{3}$

Hence,

$xy = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(x + 1\right)\dfrac{3}{2} - \sqrt{x + 1} + \dfrac{16}{3}$

So, put $x = 8$, then

$8f\left(8\right) = \dfrac{27}{3} - 3 + \dfrac{16}{3}$

$⇒ f\left(8\right) = \dfrac{34}{3 \times 8}$

$⇒ 12f\left(8\right) = 17$

questions.q: $\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{3}{n}\left\{4 + {\left(2 + \dfrac{1}{n}\right)}^{2} + {\left(2 + \dfrac{2}{n}\right)}^{2} + \ldots + {\left(3 - \dfrac{1}{n}\right)}^{2}\right\}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let

$L = \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{3}{n}\left[4 + {\left(2 + \dfrac{1}{n}\right)}^{2} + {\left(2 + \dfrac{2}{n}\right)}^{2} + . . . + {\left(3 - \dfrac{1}{n}\right)}^{2}\right]$

$⇒ L = \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{3}{n}\left[{\left(2 + \dfrac{0}{n}\right)}^{2} + {\left(2 + \dfrac{1}{n}\right)}^{2} + {\left(2 + \dfrac{2}{n}\right)}^{2} + . . . + {\left(2 + \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{n}\right)\right)}^{2}\right]$

$⇒ L = 3\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{1}{n}\left[\mathop{∑}_{r = 0}^{n - 1}{\left(2 + \dfrac{r}{n}\right)}^{2}\right]$

$⇒ L = 3{∫}_{0}^{1}{\left(2 + x\right)}^{2}dx$

$⇒ L = {\left[{\left(2 + x\right)}^{3}\right]}_{0}^{1}$

$⇒ L = 27 - 8$

$⇒ L = 19$

$I = {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}^{2}\dfrac{\tan^{- 1}x}{x} d x . . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now, let $x = \dfrac{1}{t} ⇒ dx = - \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}}dt$

questions.q:
Let $f\left(x\right) = x + \dfrac{a}{{\pi}^{2} - 4}sinx + \dfrac{b}{{\pi}^{2} - 4}cosx$, $x \in \mathbb{R}$ be a function which satisfies $f\left(x\right) = x + {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}sin\left(x + y\right)f\left(y\right)dy$. Then $\left(a + b\right)$
is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = x + {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}sin\left(x + y\right)f\left(y\right)dy$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = x + {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\left(sinxcosy + cosxsiny\right)f\left(y\right)dy$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = x + {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\left(\left(cosyf\left(y\right)dy\right)sinx + \left(sinyf\left(y\right)dy\right)cosx\right)$

And,$f\left(x\right) = x + \dfrac{a}{{\pi}^{2} - 4}sinx + \dfrac{b}{{\pi}^{2} - 4}cosx, x \in \mathbb{R}$

On comparing both the equations of $f ( x )$ we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{a}{{\pi}^{2} - 4} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}cosyf\left(y\right)dy \ldots \left(1\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{b}{{\pi}^{2} - 4} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}sinyf\left(y\right)dy \ldots \left(2\right)$

Adding equation $\left(1\right)$ and equation $\left(2\right)$ we get,

$\dfrac{a + b}{{\pi}^{2} - 4} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\left(siny + cosy\right)f\left(y\right)dy \ldots \left(3\right)$

$∵ {∫}_{0}^{a}f ( x ) d x = {∫}_{0}^{a}f ( a - x ) d x$

$∴ \dfrac{a + b}{{\pi}^{2} - 4} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\left(siny + cosy\right)f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - y\right)dy \ldots \left(4\right)$

Add equation $\left(3\right)$ and equation $\left(4\right)$ we get,

$\dfrac{2\left(a + b\right)}{{\pi}^{2} - 4} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\left(siny + cosy\right)\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} + \dfrac{\left(a + b\right)}{{\pi}^{2} - 4}\left(siny + cosy\right)\right)dy$

$⇒ \dfrac{2\left(a + b\right)}{{\pi}^{2} - 4} = \pi + \dfrac{a + b}{{\pi}^{2} - 4}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} + 1\right)$

$⇒ \left(a + b\right) = - 2\pi\left(\pi + 2\right)$

questions.q: Let [x] denote the greatest integer $\le x$. Consider the function $f ( x ) = max\left\{{x}^{2}, 1 + [ x ]\right\}$. Then the value of the integral ${∫}_{0}^{2}f ( x ) dx$ is :
questions.solution:
Plotting the diagram of the given function $f ( x ) = max\left\{{x}^{2}, 1 + [ x ]\right\}$ we get,

Now when $x \in [ 0, 1 ) ⇒ f\left(x\right) = 1$

When $x \in [ 1, \sqrt{2} ) ⇒ f\left(x\right) = 2$

And when $x \in \left[\sqrt{2}, 2\right] ⇒ f\left(x\right) = {x}^{2}$

So, from above diagram area can be calculated as,

$A = {∫}_{0}^{1}1 . dx + {∫}_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}2dx + {∫}_{\sqrt{2}}^{2}{x}^{2}dx$

$⇒ A = 1 + 2\sqrt{2} - 2 + \dfrac{8}{3} - \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}$

$⇒ A = \dfrac{5}{3} + \dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{3}$

questions.q: If ${∫}_{\dfrac{1}{3}}^{3}\left|{\log}_{e}x\right|dx = \dfrac{m}{n}{\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{{n}^{2}}{e}\right)$, where $m$ and $n$ are coprime natural numbers, then ${m}^{2} + {n}^{2} - 5$ is equal to _____ .
questions.solution:
Let

$I = {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{3}}^{3}\left|lnx\right|dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{3}}^{1}\left|lnx\right|dx + {∫}_{1}^{3}\left|lnx\right|dx$

$⇒ I = - {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{3}}^{1}lnxdx + {∫}_{1}^{3}lnxdx$

Since, $lnx < 0forx \in \left(0, 1\right)$.

$⇒ I = - {\left[xlnx - x\right]}_{\dfrac{1}{3}}^{1} + {\left[xlnx - x\right]}_{1}^{3}$

$⇒ I = - \left[\left(0 - 1\right) - \left(- \dfrac{1}{3}ln3 - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\right] + \left[3ln3 - 3 - \left(0 - 1\right)\right]$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{2}{3} - \dfrac{1}{3}ln3 + 3ln3 - 2$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{8}{3}ln3 - \dfrac{4}{3}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{4}{3}\left(2ln3 - 1\right)$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{4}{3}\left(ln{3}^{2} - lne\right)$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{4}{3}ln\left(\dfrac{{3}^{2}}{e}\right)$

So, $m = 4, n = 3$

Hence, ${m}^{2} + {n}^{2} - 5 = 16 + 9 - 5 = 20$

questions.q: The minimum value of the function $f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{2}{e}^{\left|x - t\right|}dt$ is
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{2}{e}^{\left|x - t\right|}dt$

Now For $x \le 0$

$f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{2}{e}^{t - x}dt = {e}^{- x}\left({e}^{2} - 1\right)$

And for $0 < x < 2$

$f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}{e}^{x - t}dt + {∫}_{x}^{2}{e}^{t - x}dt = {e}^{x} + {e}^{2 - x} - 2$

For $x \ge 2$

$f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{2}{e}^{x - t}dt = {e}^{x - 2}\left({e}^{2} - 1\right)$

Now for $x \le 0, f\left(x\right)$ is decreasing as ${e}^{- x}$ is decreasing function and $x \ge 2, f\left(x\right)$ is increasing as ${e}^{x - 2}$ is increasing function,

So, minimum value of $f\left(x\right)$ lies in $x \in \left(0, 2\right)$

Applying A.M $\ge$ G.M in ${e}^{x} + {e}^{2 - x}$we get,

$\dfrac{{e}^{x} + {e}^{2 - x}}{2} \ge \sqrt{{e}^{x} \times {e}^{2 - x}}$

$⇒ {e}^{x} + {e}^{2 - x} \ge 2e$

Hence, the minimum value of $f\left(x\right)$ is $2e - 2 = 2\left(e - 1\right)$

questions.solution:
Given integration is

${∫}_{\dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}}^{\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{4}}\dfrac{48}{\sqrt{9 - 4{x}^{2}}}dx$

We know that

$∫ \dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{{a}^{2} - {x}^{2}}} = \sin^{- 1}\dfrac{x}{a} + C$

So, the equation can be re-written as

${∫}_{\dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}}^{\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{4}}\dfrac{48}{2\sqrt{{\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)}^{2} - {x}^{2}}}dx = \dfrac{48}{2} \times {\left[\sin^{- 1}\dfrac{2x}{3}\right]}_{\dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}}^{\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{4}}$

$= 24 \times \left[\sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{4}\right) - \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}\right)\right]$

$= 24 \times \left[\sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) - \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\right]$

$= 24 \times \left[\dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right] = 2\pi$

questions.q: Let $f$ be a differentiable function defined on $\left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$ such that $f\left(x\right) > 0$ and $f\left(x\right) + {∫}_{0}^{x}f\left(t\right)\sqrt{1 - {\left({\log}_{e}\left(f\left(t\right)\right)\right)}^{2}}dt = e ∀ x \in \left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$, then ${\left\{6{\log}_{e}\left(f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)\right\}}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given:

$f\left(x\right) + {∫}_{0}^{x}f\left(t\right)\sqrt{1 - {\left({\log}_{e}\left(f\left(t\right)\right)\right)}^{2}}dt = e . . . \left(1\right)$

Put $x = 0$, then

$f\left(0\right) = e$.

Differentiating $\left(1\right)$ w.r.t. $x$, we get

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) + f\left(x\right)\sqrt{1 - {\left({\log}_{e}\left(f\left(x\right)\right)\right)}^{2}} = 0$

Put $y = f\left(x\right)$.

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y\sqrt{1 - {\left({\log}_{e}y\right)}^{2}} = 0$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{dy}{y\sqrt{1 - {\left({\log}_{e}y\right)}^{2}}} = - ∫ dx$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{d\left({\log}_{e}y\right)}{\sqrt{1 - {\left({\log}_{e}y\right)}^{2}}} = - ∫ dx$

$⇒ \sin^{- 1}\left({\log}_{e}y\right) = - x + C$

Put $x = 0, y = e$

$\sin^{- 1}\left({\log}_{e}e\right) = - 0 + C$

$⇒ C = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

So,

$\sin^{- 1}\left({\log}_{e}y\right) = - x + \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$⇒ {\log}_{e}y = sin\left(- x + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

$⇒ {\log}_{e}f\left(x\right) = sin\left(- x + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

Put $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$⇒ {\log}_{e}f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = sin\left(- \dfrac{\pi}{6} + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$⇒ 6{\log}_{e}f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = 3\sqrt{3}$

$⇒ {\left\{6{\log}_{e}f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right\}}^{2} = 27$

questions.q: The value of $12{∫}_{0}^{3}\left|{x}^{2} - 3x + 2\right|dx$ is ______
questions.solution:
$I = {∫}_{0}^{3}\left|{x}^{2} - 3x + 2\right|dx$

$= {∫}_{0}^{3}\left|\left(x - 1\right)\left(x - 2\right)\right|dx$

$= {∫}_{0}^{1}\left({x}^{2} - 3x + 2\right)dx - {∫}_{1}^{2}\left({x}^{2} - 3x + 2\right)dx + {∫}_{2}^{3}\left({x}^{2} - 3x + 2\right)dx$

$= {\left[\dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3} - 3\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right) + 2x\right]}_{0}^{1} - {\left[\dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3} - 3\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right) + 2x\right]}_{1}^{2} + {\left[\dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3} - 3\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right) + 2x\right]}_{2}^{3}$

$= \left(\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{3}{2} + 2\right) - \left[\left(\dfrac{8}{3} - 6 + 4\right) - \left(\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{3}{2} + 2\right)\right] + \left[\left(9 - \dfrac{27}{2} + 6\right) - \left(\dfrac{8}{3} - 6 + 4\right)\right]$

$= \left(\dfrac{2}{3} - 3 + 4\right) - \left(\dfrac{16}{3} - 12 + 8\right) + \left(9 - \dfrac{27}{2} + 6\right)$

$= 20 - \dfrac{109}{6} = \dfrac{11}{6}$

So,

$12I = 12 \times \dfrac{11}{6} = 22$

$I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{2}{3}}\left[- 3{x}^{2} + 7x - 2\right]dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{2}{3}}^{1}\left(3{x}^{2} - 3x + 2\right)dx + 1$

Let ${I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{2}{3}}\left[- 3{x}^{2} + 7x - 2\right]dx$

The graph of $y = - 3{x}^{2} + 7x - 2$ and

${I}_{2} = {∫}_{\dfrac{2}{3}}^{1}\left(3{x}^{2} - 3x + 2\right)dx$

So ${I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{\alpha}\left(- 2\right)dx + {∫}_{\alpha}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}\left(- 1\right)dx + {∫}_{1 / 3}^{\beta}0dx + {∫}_{\beta}^{\dfrac{2}{3}}1 \cdot dx$

$= - 2\alpha - \left(\dfrac{1}{3} - \alpha\right) + \dfrac{2}{3} - \beta = - \alpha - \beta + \dfrac{1}{3}$

$y = 3{x}^{2} - 3x + 2$

When $x \in \left(\dfrac{2}{3}, 1\right)$

$3{x}^{2} - 3x + 2 \in \left(\dfrac{4}{3}, 2\right)$

$\left[3{x}^{2} - 3x + 2\right] = 1$

$∴ {I}_{2} = {∫}_{\dfrac{2}{3}}^{1}\left[3{x}^{2} - 3x + 2\right]dx = 1\left(1 - \dfrac{2}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Hence $I = \left(\dfrac{1}{3} - ( \alpha + \beta )\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) + 1$

$= \dfrac{5}{3} - \left(\dfrac{7 - \sqrt{37}}{6} + \dfrac{7 - \sqrt{13}}{6}\right)$

$= \dfrac{- 2}{3} + \dfrac{\sqrt{37} + \sqrt{13}}{6}$= \dfrac{- 2}{3} + \dfrac{\sqrt{37} + \sqrt{13}}{6}$

$= \dfrac{\sqrt{37} + \sqrt{13} - 4}{6}$

questions.q: If $f\left(\alpha\right) = {∫}_{1}^{\alpha}\dfrac{{\log}_{10}t}{1 + t}dt, \alpha > 0$, then $f\left({e}^{3}\right) + f\left({e}^{- 3}\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(\alpha\right) = {∫}_{1}^{\alpha}\dfrac{{\log}_{10}t}{1 + t}dt$

So, $f\left({e}^{3}\right) = {∫}_{1}^{{e}^{3}}\dfrac{lnt}{ln10\left(1 + t\right)}dt ⋯ \left(1\right)$

Again $f\left(\alpha\right) = {∫}_{1}^{\alpha}\dfrac{lnt}{\left(ln10\right)\left(1 + t\right)}dt$

Now let $t = \dfrac{1}{x} ⇒ x = \dfrac{1}{t}⇒ dt = \dfrac{- 1}{{x}^{2}}dx$

So, $f\left(\alpha\right) = {∫}_{1}^{\dfrac{1}{a}}\dfrac{- lnnx}{\left(ln10\right)\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)}\left(- \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}}\right)dx$

$⇒ f\left(\alpha\right) = \dfrac{1}{ln10}{∫}_{1}^{\dfrac{1}{\alpha}}\dfrac{lnx}{x\left(x + 1\right)}dx$

So, $f\left({e}^{- 3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{ln10}{∫}_{1}^{{e}^{3}}\dfrac{lnt}{t\left(t + 1\right)}dt \ldots \left(2\right)$

Now adding equation $\left(1\right)$ and $\left(2\right)$ we get,

$f\left({e}^{3}\right) + f\left({e}^{- 3}\right)= \left(\dfrac{1}{lnn10}\right){∫}_{1}^{{c}^{3}}\dfrac{lnt}{\left(1 + t\right)}\left[1 + \dfrac{1}{t}\right]dt$

$⇒ f\left({e}^{3}\right) + f\left({e}^{- 3}\right) = \left(\dfrac{1}{ln10}\right){∫}_{1}^{3}\dfrac{lnt}{t}dt$

Now let $lnt = r⇒ \dfrac{dt}{t} = dr$

So, $f\left({e}^{3}\right) + f\left({e}^{- 3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{ln10}{∫}_{0}^{3}rdr$

$⇒ f\left({e}^{3}\right) + f\left({e}^{- 3}\right){= \left(\dfrac{1}\ln10\right)\left(\dfrac{{r}^{2}}{2}\right)}_{0}^{3}$

$⇒ f\left({e}^{3}\right) + f\left({e}^{- 3}\right) = \left(\dfrac{1}{log10}\right)\left(\dfrac{9}{2}\right)$

$⇒ f\left({e}^{3}\right) + f\left({e}^{- 3}\right) = \dfrac{9}{2{\log}_{e}10}$

questions.q: Let ${I}_{n}\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{1}{{\left({t}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}}dt, n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots .$ Then
questions.solution:
Given,

${I}_{n}\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{dt}{{\left({t}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}}$

Applying integration by parts we get,

$⇒ {I}_{n}\left(x\right) = {\left[\dfrac{t}{{\left({t}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}}\right]}_{0}^{x} - {∫}_{0}^{x}n{\left({t}^{2} + 5\right)}^{- n - 1} \cdot 2{t}^{2}$

$⇒ {I}_{n}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x}{{\left({x}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}} + 2n{∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{{t}^{2}}{{\left({t}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n + 1}}dt$

$⇒ {I}_{n}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x}{{\left({x}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}} + 2n{∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{\left({t}^{2} + 5\right) - 5}{{\left({t}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n + 1}}dt$

$⇒ {I}_{n}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x}{{\left({x}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}} + 2n{∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{dt}{{\left({t}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}} - 10n{∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{dt}{{\left({t}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n + 1}}$

$⇒ {I}_{n}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x}{{\left({x}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}} + 2n{I}_{n}\left(x\right) - 10n{I}_{n + 1}\left(x\right)$

$⇒ 10n{I}_{n + 1}\left(x\right) + \left(1 - 2n\right){I}_{n}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x}{{\left({x}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}}$

$⇒ 10n{I}_{n + 1}\left(x\right) + \left(1 - 2n\right){I}_{n}\left(x\right) = x{I}^{'}n$ {where ${I}^{'}n = \dfrac{1}{{\left({x}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}}$ we get by differentiating ${I}_{n}\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{dt}{{\left({t}^{2} + 5\right)}^{n}}$ }

Now put $n = 5$

We get, $50{I}_{6} - 9{I}_{5} = x{I}_{5}^{'}$

questions.q: The value of the integral ${∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}60\dfrac{sin\left(6x\right)}{sinx}dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}60\dfrac{sin6x}{sinx}dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}60\dfrac{2sin3xcos3x}{sinx}dx$

$⇒ I = 60{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2\left(3sinx - 4\sin^{3}x\right)\left(4\cos^{3}x - 3cosx\right)}{sinx}dx$

$⇒ I = 120{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(3 - 4\sin^{2}x\right)\left(4\cos^{2}x - 3\right)cosxdx$

$⇒ I = 120{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(3 - 4\sin^{2}x\right)\left(1 - 4\sin^{2}x\right)cosxdx$

Now let $sinx = t ⇒ cosxdx = dt$ and limit changes to $0\text{to}1$,

So, $I = 120{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(3 - 4{t}^{2}\right)\left(1 - 4{t}^{2}\right)dt$

$⇒ I = 120{∫}_{0}^{1}3 - 16{t}^{2} + 16{t}^{4}dt$

$⇒ I = 120{\left[3t - \dfrac{16{t}^{3}}{3} + \dfrac{16{t}^{5}}{5}\right]}_{0}^{1}$

$⇒ I = 120\left[3 - \dfrac{16}{3} + \dfrac{16}{5}\right] = 120 \times \dfrac{45 - 80 + 48}{15} = 8 \times 13 = 104$

questions.q: The minimum value of the twice differentiable function $f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}{e}^{x - t}{f}^{'}\left(t\right)dt - \left({x}^{2} - x + 1\right){e}^{x}, x \in R$, is
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}{e}^{x - t}{f}^{'}\left(t\right)dt - \left({x}^{2} - x + 1\right){e}^{x}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = {e}^{x}{∫}_{0}^{x}{e}^{- t}{f}^{'}\left(t\right)dt - \left({x}^{2} - x + 1\right){e}^{x}$

questions.solution:
Given,

${∫}_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}\dfrac{15{x}^{3}}{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{2} + \sqrt{{\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right)}^{3}}}}dx = \alpha\sqrt{2} + \beta\sqrt{3}$,

Taking L.H.S we get ${∫}_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}\dfrac{15{x}^{3}}{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{2} + \sqrt{{\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right)}^{3}}}}dx$

Now put $1 + {x}^{2} = {t}^{2}$

$⇒ 2xdx = 2tdt$

$⇒ xdt = tdt$

$∴ {∫}_{1}^{2}\dfrac{15\left({t}^{2} - 1\right)tdt}{\sqrt{{t}^{2} + {t}^{3}}}$

$= 15{∫}_{1}^{2}\dfrac{t\left({t}^{2} - 1\right)}{t\sqrt{1 + t}}dt$

Now put $1 + t = {u}^{2}$⇒ dt = 2udu$

So, the integral will be $15{∫}_{\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{3}}\dfrac{{\left({u}^{2} - 1\right)}^{2} - 1}{u} \times 2udu$

$= 30{∫}_{\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{3}}\left({u}^{4} - 2{u}^{2}\right)du$

$= 30{\left(\dfrac{{u}^{5}}{5} - \dfrac{2{u}^{3}}{3}\right)}_{\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{3}}$

$= 30\left[\dfrac{1}{5}\left(9\sqrt{3} - 4\sqrt{2}\right) - \dfrac{2}{3}\left(3\sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{2}\right)\right]$

$= 30\left[- \dfrac{1}{5} \times \sqrt{3} + \dfrac{8}{15}\sqrt{2}\right]$

$= - 6\sqrt{3} + 16\sqrt{2}$

So, ${∫}_{0}^{\sqrt{4}}\dfrac{15{x}^{3}}{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{2} + \sqrt{{\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right)}^{3}}}}dx = \alpha\sqrt{2} + \beta\sqrt{3}$

$⇒ - 6\sqrt{3} + 16\sqrt{2} = \alpha\sqrt{2} + \beta\sqrt{3}$

Now on comparing we get, $\alpha = 16, \beta = - 6$

$∴ \alpha + \beta = 10$

questions.solution:

Now finding ${∫}_{0}^{10}f\left(x\right) \cdot dx = - 10 - 9 - 8 - \ldots . . - 1$

$= \dfrac{10 \cdot 11 \cdot 21}{6} = 385$

And ${∫}_{0}^{10}\left|f\left(x\right)\right| = 10 + 9 + 8 + \ldots . + 1$

$= \dfrac{10 \cdot 11}{2} = 55$

So, ${∫}_{0}^{10}f\left(x\right)dx + {∫}_{0}^{10}{\left(f\left(x\right)\right)}^{2}dx + {∫}_{0}^{10}\left|f\left(x\right)\right|dx$

$= - 55 + 385 + 55 = 385$

questions.q: Let $f$ be a differentiable function satisfying $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}{∫}_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}f\left(\dfrac{{\lambda}^{2}x}{3}\right)d\lambda, x > 0$ and $f\left(1\right) = \sqrt{3}$. If $y = f\left(x\right)$ passes through the point $\left(\alpha, 6\right)$, then $\alpha$ is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}{∫}_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}f\left(\dfrac{{\lambda}^{2}x}{3}\right)d\lambda$

Now let $\dfrac{{\lambda}^{2}x}{3} = t$

$⇒ \dfrac{2\lambdax}{3}d\lambda = dt$

$⇒ d\lambda = \dfrac{3}{2} \cdot \dfrac{1\sqrt{x}}{x \cdot \sqrt{3}\sqrt{t}}dt$

$⇒ d\lambda = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}} \cdot \dfrac{dt}{\sqrt{t}}$

So, $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}{∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{f\left(t\right)}{\sqrt{t}}dt$

$\sqrt{x}f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{f\left(t\right)}{\sqrt{t}}dt$

Now differentiating both side we get,

$⇒ \sqrt{x} \cdot {f}^{'}\left(x\right) + \dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{2\sqrt{x}} = \dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{\sqrt{x}}$

$⇒ \sqrt{x} \cdot {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{2\sqrt{x}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{y} = \dfrac{dx}{2x}$

Now integrating both side we get,

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{dy}{y} = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{2x}$

$⇒ lny = \dfrac{1}{2}lnx + lnc$

Given $f\left(1\right) = \sqrt{3}$, so $⇒ ln\sqrt{3} = 0 + lnc$

$⇒ c = \sqrt{3}$

So, $f\left(x\right) = \sqrt{3x}$

Now given $f\left(x\right)$ is passing through $\left(\alpha, 6\right)$,

So $f\left(\alpha\right) = 6 ⇒ 36 = 3\alpha$

$⇒ \alpha = 12$

questions.solution:
Let, $f\left(x\right) = 8sinx - sin2x$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 8cosx - 2cos2x$

$⇒ {f}^{' '}\left(x\right) = - 8sinx + 4sin2x$

$⇒ {f}^{' '}\left(x\right) = - 8sinx\left(1 - cosx\right)$

So, ${f}^{'}\left(x\right) < 0\text{when}x \in \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}, \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$

Hence ${f}^{'}\left(x\right)$ is decreasing function in given domain,

Now, ${f}^{'}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) < {f}^{'}\left(x\right) < {f}^{'}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$

$⇒ 5 < {f}^{'}\left(x\right) < \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ 5 < {f}^{'}\left(x\right) < 4\sqrt{2}$

Now integrating all with respect to $dx$

$∫ 5dx < ∫ {f}^{'}\left(x\right)dx < ∫ 4\sqrt{2}dx$

$⇒ 5x < f\left(x\right) < 4\sqrt{2}x$

$⇒ 5 < \dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{x} < 4\sqrt{2}$

Again integrating with ${∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}$

We get, ${∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}5 < ∫ \dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{x} < {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}4\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}5 < ∫ \dfrac{8sinx - sin2x}{x} < {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}4\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{5\pi}{12} < I < \dfrac{\sqrt{2}\pi}{3}$

questions.q: If $a = \lim_{n \to \infty}\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}\dfrac{2n}{{n}^{2} + {k}^{2}}$ and $f\left(x\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - cosx}{1 + cosx}}, x \in \left(0, 1\right)$, then:
questions.solution:
Given, $a = \lim_{n \to \infty}\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}\dfrac{2n}{{n}^{2} + {k}^{2}}$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{n}\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}\dfrac{2}{1 + {\left(\dfrac{k}{n}\right)}^{2}} = {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{2}{1 + {x}^{2}}dx$

$⇒ a = 2{\left[\tan^{- 1}x\right]}_{0}^{1}$

$⇒ a = 2\left[\dfrac{\pi}{4} - 0\right] = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

Now, $f\left(x\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - cosx}{1 + cosx}}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right); x \in \left(0, 1\right)$

So, $f\left(\dfrac{a}{2}\right) = f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$

$⇒ f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \sqrt{2} - 1$

And ${f}^{'}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}{sec}^{2}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{8}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2} + 1}$

So, ${f}^{'}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \sqrt{2}f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$

questions.solution:
Given, ${∫}_{- 3}^{101}\left(\left[sin\pix\right] + {e}^{\left[cos2\pix\right]}\right)dx$

Now let ${I}_{1} = {∫}_{- 3}^{101}\left[sin\pix\right]dx$ and ${I}_{2} = {∫}_{- 3}^{101}{e}^{\left[cos2\pix\right]}dx$

Now checking periodicity of $\left[sin\pix\right]$ we get,

$0 < x < 1 ⇒ \left[sin\pix\right] = 0$

$1 < x < 2 ⇒ \left[sin\pix\right] = - 1$

$\left[sin\pix\right] \to$ periodic with period 2

So, ${I}_{1} = 52{∫}_{0}^{2}\left[sin\pix\right]dx$

$= 52\left[{∫}_{0}^{1}0 + {∫}_{1}^{2} - 1dx\right] = - 52$

Now checking periodicity of $\left[cos2\pix\right]$ we get,

$0 < x < \dfrac{1}{4} ⇒ \left[cos2\pix\right] = 0$

$\dfrac{1}{4} < x < \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ \left[cos2\pix\right] = - 1$

$\dfrac{1}{2} < x < \dfrac{3}{4} ⇒ \left[cos2\pix\right] = - 1$

$\dfrac{3}{4} < x < 1 ⇒ \left[cos2\pix\right] = 0$

So, $\left[cos2\pix\right]$ has periodicity of $1$

So, ${I}_{2} = 104\left({∫}_{0}^${$\dfrac{1}{4}$}${e}^{0}dx + {∫}_${$\dfrac{1}{4}$}$^${$\dfrac{3}{4}$}${e}^{- 1}dx + {∫}_${$\dfrac{3}{4}$}$^{1}{e}^{0}dx\right)

$⇒ {I}_{2} = 104$\left(\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{e} \times \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{4}\right)$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = 52 + \dfrac{52}{e}$

So, ${I}_{1} + {I}_{2} = \dfrac{52}{e}$ or ${∫}_{- 3}^{101}\left(\left[sin\pix\right] + {e}^{\left[cos2\pix\right]}\right)dx = \dfrac{52}{e}$

questions.q: Let $f$ be a twice differentiable function on $R$. If ${f}^{'}\left(0\right) = 4$ and $f\left(x\right) + {∫}_{0}^{x}\left(x - t\right){f}^{'}\left(t\right)dt$= \left({e}^{2x} + {e}^{- 2x}\right)cos2x + \dfrac{2}{a}x$, then ${\left(2a + 1\right)}^{5}{a}^{2}$ is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) + {∫}_{0}^{x}\left(x - t\right){f}^{'}\left(t\right)dt = \left({e}^{2x} + {e}^{- 2x}\right)cos2x + \dfrac{2x}{a} ⋯ \left(i\right)$

Putting $x = 0$ both side we get, $f\left(0\right) = 2 ⋯ \left(ii\right)$

On differentiating equation $\left(i\right)$ w.r.t. $x$ we get:

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) + {∫}_{0}^{x}{f}^{'}\left(t\right)dt + x{f}^{'}\left(x\right) - x{f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 2\left({e}^{2x} - {e}^{- 2x}\right)cos2x - 2\left({e}^{2x} + {e}^{- 2x}\right)sin2x + \dfrac{2}{a}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) + f\left(x\right) - f\left(0\right) = 2\left({e}^{2x} - {e}^{- 2x}\right)cos2x - 2\left({e}^{2x} + {e}^{- 2x}\right)sin2x + \dfrac{2}{a}$

Replace $x$ by $0$ we get:

$⇒ 4 = \dfrac{2}{a} ⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Now putting the value of $a$ in${\left(2a + 1\right)}^{5} \cdot {a}^{2}$

We get, ${2}^{5} \cdot \dfrac{1}{{2}^{2}} = {2}^{3} = 8$

For any real number $x$, let $\left[x\right]$ denote the largest integer less than or equal to $x$. Let $f$ be a real-valued function defined on the interval $\left[- 10, 10\right]$ by

$f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}x - \left[x\right], & \text{if}\left[x\right]\text{is odd} \\ 1 + \left[x\right] - x, & \text{if}\left[x\right]\text{is even}\end{cases}\right$

Then, the value of $\dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{10}{∫}_{- 10}^{10}f\left(x\right)cos \pixdx$ is
questions.solution:
$f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}x - 1, \\ 1 - x,\end{array}\begin{array}{ll}1 \le x < 2 \\ 0 \le x < 1\end{array}\right$

$f\left(x\right)$ is periodic with period $2$, and is even.

$∴ I = {∫}_{- 10}^{10}f\left(x\right)cos \pixdx$

$= 2{∫}_{0}^{10}f\left(x\right)cos \pixdx$

$= 2 \times 5{∫}_{0}^{2}f\left(x\right)cos \pixdx$

$= 10\left[{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(1 - x\right)cos \pixdx + {∫}_{1}^{2}\left(x - 1\right)cos \pixdx\right] = 10\left({I}_{1} + {I}_{2}\right)$

${I}_{2} = {∫}_{1}^{2}\left(x - 1\right)cos \pixdx$

Put $\left(x - 1\right) = t$

${I}_{2} = - {∫}_{0}^{1}tcos \pitdt$

${I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(1 - x\right)cos \pixdx = - {∫}_{0}^{1}xcos\left(\pix\right)dx$

$∴ I = 10\left[- 2{∫}_{0}^{1}xcos \pixdx\right] = - 20{\left[x\dfrac{sin \pix}{\pi} + \dfrac{cos \pix}{{\pi}^{2}}\right]}_{0}^{1}$

$= - 20\left[- \dfrac{1}{{\pi}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{\pi}^{2}}\right] = \dfrac{40}{{\pi}^{2}}$

$∴ \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{10}I = 4$

questions.q: If $\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{{\left(n + 1\right)}^{k - 1}}{{n}^{k + 1}}\left[( nk + 1 ) + ( nk + 2 ) + \ldots + \left(nk + n\right)\right] = 33$ . $\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{1}{{n}^{k + 1}} \cdot \left[{1}^{k} + {2}^{k} + {3}^{k} + \ldots + {n}^{k}\right]$, then the integral value of $k$ is equal to _____ .
questions.solution:
Given,

$\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{{\left(n + 1\right)}^{k - 1}}{{n}^{k + 1}}\left[( nk + 1 ) + ( nk + 2 ) + \ldots + \left(nk + n\right)\right] = 33$

Taking $LHS$

$\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{{\left(n + 1\right)}^{k - 1}}{{n}^{k + 1}}\left[nk \cdot n + 1 + 2 + \ldots + n\right]$

$= \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{{\left(n + 1\right)}^{{}^{k - 1}}}{{n}^{k + 1}} \cdot \left[{n}^{2}k + \dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2}\right]$

$= \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{{\left(n + 1\right)}^{k - 1} \cdot {n}^{2}\left(k + \dfrac{\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{n}\right)}{2}\right)}{{n}^{k + 1}}$

$= \lim_{n \to \infty}\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{n}\right)\left(k + \dfrac{\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{n}\right)}{2}\right)$

$= \left(k + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

Now taking $RHS$

$= 33\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{1}{{n}^{k + 1}}\left({1}^{k} + {2}^{k} + \ldots + {n}^{k}\right) = 33\lim_{n \to \infty}\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}\dfrac{1}{n}{\left(\dfrac{k}{n}\right)}^{k}$

$= 33{∫}_{0}^{1}{x}^{k}dx = \dfrac{33}{k + 1}$

Now given, $LHS = RHS$

$⇒ k + \dfrac{1}{2} = 33 \cdot \dfrac{1}{k + 1}$

$⇒ \left(2k + 1\right)\left(k + 1\right) = 66$

$⇒ \left(k - 5\right)\left(2k + 13\right) = 0$

$⇒ k =5$ or $- \dfrac{13}{2}$

So, integral value of $k = 5$

questions.q: Let $f$ be a real valued continuous function on $\left[0, 1\right]$ and $f\left(x\right) = x + {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(x - t\right)f\left(t\right)dt$. Then which of the following points $\left(x, y\right)$ lies on the curve $y = f \left(x\right)?$
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = x\left(1 + {∫}_{0}^{1}f\left(t\right)dt\right) - {∫}_{0}^{1}tf\left(t\right)dt$

$f\left(x\right) = Ax - B . . . \left(i\right)$

A = 1 + {∫}_{0}^{1}f$\left(t\right)$dt = 1 + {∫}_{0}^{1}$\left(At - B\right)$dt$

$⇒ A = 2$\left(1 - B\right)$ . . . $\left(ii\right)$

Also $B = {∫}_{0}^{1}tf\left(t\right)$dt = {∫}_{0}^{1}$\left(A{t}^{2} - Bt\right)$dt$

A = \dfrac{9}{2}B . . . \left(iii\right)

From \left(ii\right)$, $\left(iii\right)

A = \dfrac{18}{13}, B = \dfrac{4}{13}$

So, $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{18}{13}x - \dfrac{4}{13}$

$⇒ f\left(6\right) = \dfrac{18 \times 6 - 4}{13} = 8$

questions.q: Let $f: R \to R$ be a differentiable function such that $f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \sqrt{2}, f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 0$ and ${f}^{'}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 1$ and let $g\left(x\right) = {∫}_{x}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\left({f}^{'}\left(t\right)sect + tantsectf\left(t\right)\right)dt$ for $x \in \left[\dfrac{\pi}{4}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) .$ Then $\lim_{x \to {\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{-}}g\left(x\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$g\left(x\right) = {∫}_{x}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\left({f}^{'}\left(t\right)sect + tantsectf\left(t\right)\right)dt$

$⇒ g\left(x\right) = {∫}_{x}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}d\left(f\left(t\right) \cdot sect\right)$⇒ g\left(x\right) = {\left[f\left(t\right)sect\right]}_{x}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}$

$g\left(x\right) = f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)sec\dfrac{\pi}{4} - f\left(x\right) \cdot secx$

$g\left(x\right) = 2 - f\left(x\right)secx = 2 - \left(\dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{cosx}\right)$

Now taking limit both side, we get

$\lim_{x \to {\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{-}}g\left(x\right) = 2 - \lim_{x \to {\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{-}}\left(\dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{cosx}\right)$

Using L'Hospital Rule

$= 2 - \lim_{x \to {\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{-}}\dfrac{{f}^{'}\left(x\right)}{\left(- sinx\right)}$

$= 2 + \dfrac{{f}^{'}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}{sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}} = 2 + \dfrac{1}{1} = 3$

questions.q: Let $f: R \to R$ be continuous function satisfying $f\left(x\right) + f\left(x + k\right) = n$, for all $x \in R$ where $k > 0$ and $n$ is a positive integer. If ${I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{4nk}f\left(x\right)dx$ and ${I}_{2} = {∫}_{- k}^{3k}f\left(x\right)dx$, then
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) + f\left(x + k\right) = n$ ....(i)

Replacing $x \to x + k$ in above equation we get,

$f\left(x + k\right) + f\left(x + 2k\right) = n$ .....(ii)

Subtraction equation (i) from equation (ii) we get,

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = f\left(x + 2k\right)$

$f\left(x\right)$ is periodic with period $2k$

Now, ${I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{4nk}f\left(x\right)dx = 2n{∫}_{0}^{2k}f\left(x\right)dx$

${I}_{2} = {∫}_{- k}^{3k}f\left(x\right)dx = 2{∫}_{0}^{2k}f\left(x\right)dx$

Now integrating both side of $f\left(x\right) + f\left(x + k\right) = n$ with limit ${∫}_{0}^{k}$ we get,

$⇒ {∫}_{0}^{k}f\left(x\right)dx + {∫}_{0}^{k}f\left(x + k\right)dx = nk$

$⇒ {∫}_{0}^{k}f\left(x\right)dx + {∫}_{k}^{2k}f\left(x\right)dx = nk$

$⇒ {∫}_{0}^{2k}f\left(x\right)dx = nk$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = 2{n}^{2}k, {I}_{2} = 2nk$

$⇒ {I}_{1} + n{I}_{2} = 4{n}^{2}k$

questions.solution:
The graph of $y = - 8{x}^{2} + 6x - 1$ will be as shown

Now ${∫}_{0}^{1}\left[- 8{x}^{2} + 6x - 1\right]dx$= {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{4}}\left(- 1\right)dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{4}}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}\left(0\right)dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}^{\dfrac{3}{4}}\left(- 1\right)dx$

$+ {∫}_{\dfrac{3}{4}}^{\dfrac{3 + \sqrt{17}}{8}}\left(- 2\right)dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{3 + \sqrt{17}}{8}}^{1}\left(- 3\right)dx$

$= - {\left[x\right]}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{4}} + 0 - {\left[x\right]}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}^{\dfrac{3}{4}} + - 2{\left[x\right]}_{\dfrac{3}{4}}^{\dfrac{3 + \sqrt{17}}{8}} - 3{\left[x\right]}_{\dfrac{3 + \sqrt{17}}{8}}^{1}$

$= - \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{- 6 - 2\sqrt{17}}{8} + \dfrac{3}{2} - 3 + \dfrac{9 + 3\sqrt{17}}{8}$

$= \dfrac{\sqrt{17} - 13}{8}$

On differentiating, we get

$- sinx{f}^{'}\left(cosx\right) = 3{sec}^{2}x - 2{sec}^{2}xtanx$

When $cosx = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ then $secx = \sqrt{3}$, $tanx = \sqrt{2} \text{ and } sinx = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}$

Then $- \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}{f}^{'}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = 3 \times 3 - 2 \times 3\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}{f}^{'}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = 6 - \dfrac{9}{\sqrt{2}}$

questions.q: The integral ${∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{{7}^{\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]}}dx$, where $\left[\cdot\right]$ denotes the greatest integer function, is equal to
questions.solution:
$I = {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{dx}{{7}^{\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]}} = {∫}_{0}^{1}{\left(\dfrac{1}{7}\right)}^{\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]}dx$

Let $\dfrac{1}{7} = k ⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{1}{k}^{\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]}dx$

$I = {∫}_{0}^{1}{k}^{\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]}dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}^{1}{k}^{\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]}dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{3}}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}{k}^{\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]}dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{4}}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}{k}^{\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]}dx + ⋯$

$⇒ I = k\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) + {k}^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{3}\right) + {k}^{3}\left(\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{4}\right) + ⋯$

$⇒ I = \left(k + \dfrac{{k}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{k}^{3}}{3} + ⋯\right) - \dfrac{1}{k}\left(\dfrac{{k}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{k}^{3}}{3} + ⋯\right)$

$⇒ I = - ln\left(1 - k\right) - \dfrac{1}{k}\left[- ln\left(1 - k\right) - k\right]$

$⇒ I = - ln\dfrac{6}{7} - 7\left[- ln\dfrac{6}{7} - \dfrac{1}{7}\right]\left(∵ k = \dfrac{1}{7}\right)$

$∴ I = 1 + 6ln\dfrac{6}{7}$

questions.q: The value of the integral ${∫}_{- 2}^{2}\dfrac{\left|{x}^{3} + x\right|}{\left({e}^{x\left|x\right|} + 1\right)}dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{\left|{x}^{3} + x\right|}{\left({e}^{x\left|x\right|} + 1\right)}dx$

and ${∫}_{- 2}^{2}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{0}^{2}\left(f\left(x\right) + f\left(- x\right)\right)dx$

$= {∫}_{0}^{2}\left(\dfrac{\left|{x}^{3} + x\right|}{\left({e}^{x\left|x\right|} + 1\right)} + \dfrac{\left|- {x}^{3} - x\right|}{\left({e}^{- x\left|- x\right|} + 1\right)}\right)dx$

$= {∫}_{0}^{2}\left(\dfrac{\left|{x}^{3} + x\right|}{\left({e}^{x\left|x\right|} + 1\right)} + \dfrac{\left|{x}^{3} + x\right|}{\left({e}^{- x\left|x\right|} + 1\right)}\right)dx$

$= {∫}_{0}^{2}\left(\dfrac{{x}^{3} + x}{\left({e}^{{x}^{2}} + 1\right)} + \dfrac{{x}^{3} + x}{\left({e}^{- {x}^{2}} + 1\right)}\right)dx$

$I = {∫}_{0}^{2}\left(\dfrac{{x}^{3} + x}{1 + {e}^{{x}^{2}}} + \dfrac{{e}^{{x}^{2}}\left({x}^{3} + x\right)}{1 + {e}^{{x}^{2}}}\right)dx$

$= {∫}_{0}^{2}\left({x}^{3} + x\right)dx$

$= {\left[\dfrac{{x}^{4}}{4} + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right]}_{0}^{2}$

$= 4 + 2 = 6$

$= {∫}_{0}^{2}\left(\dfrac{\left|{x}^{3} + x\right|}{\left({e}^{x\left|x\right|} + 1\right)} + \dfrac{\left|- {x}^{3} - x\right|}{\left({e}^{- x\left|- x\right|} + 1\right)}\right)dx$

$= {∫}_{0}^{2}\left(\dfrac{\left|{x}^{3} + x\right|}{\left({e}^{x\left|x\right|} + 1\right)} + \dfrac{\left|{x}^{3} + x\right|}{\left({e}^{- x\left|x\right|} + 1\right)}\right)dx$

$= {∫}_{0}^{2}\left(\dfrac{{x}^{3} + x}{\left({e}^{{x}^{2}} + 1\right)} + \dfrac{{x}^{3} + x}{\left({e}^{- {x}^{2}} + 1\right)}\right)dx$

$= 4 + 2 = 6$

questions.q: The integral $\dfrac{24}{\pi}{∫}_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}\dfrac{\left(2 - {x}^{2}\right)dx}{\left(2 + {x}^{2}\right)\sqrt{4 + {x}^{4}}}$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Let, $I = \dfrac{24}{\pi}{∫}_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}\dfrac{2 - {x}^{2}}{\left(2 + {x}^{2}\right)\left(\sqrt{4 + {x}^{4}}\right)}dx$

$= \dfrac{24}{\pi}{∫}_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}\dfrac{2 - {x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}\left(\dfrac{2}{x} + x\right)\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{4}{{x}^{2}} + {x}^{2}\right)}}dx$

$= \dfrac{24}{\pi}{∫}_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}\dfrac{\dfrac{2}{{x}^{2}} - 1}{\left(\dfrac{2}{x} + x\right)\sqrt{{\left(\dfrac{2}{x} + x\right)}^{2} - 4}}dx$

Now let $\dfrac{2}{x} + x = t, \left(- \dfrac{2}{{x}^{2}} + 1\right)dx = dt$

$I = - \dfrac{24}{\pi}{∫}_{\infty}^{2\sqrt{2}}\dfrac{dt}{t\sqrt{{t}^{2} - 4}} = - \dfrac{12}{\pi}{∫}_{\infty}^{2\sqrt{2}}\dfrac{2tdt}{{t}^{2}\sqrt{{t}^{2} - 4}}$

Let ${t}^{2} - 4 = {z}^{2}, 2tdt = 2zdz$

$I = - \dfrac{12}{\pi}{∫}_{\infty}^{2}\dfrac{2zdz}{z\left({z}^{2} + 4\right)} = - \dfrac{24}{\pi}{∫}_{\infty}^{2}\dfrac{dz}{\left({z}^{2} + 4\right)} = - \dfrac{24}{\pi}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{z}{2}\right)}_{\infty}^{2}$

$= - \dfrac{24}{\pi}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{8} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 3$

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = max\left\{\left|x + 1\right|, \left|x + 2\right|, \ldots , \left|x + 5\right|\right\}$. Then ${∫}_{- 6}^{0}f\left(x\right)dx$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
$f\left(x\right) =$ max $\left\{\left|x + 1\right|, \left|x + 2\right|, \left|x + 3\right|, \left|x + 4\right|, \left|x + 5\right|\right\}$

${∫}_{- 6}^{0}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{- 6}^{- 3}\left|x + 1\right|dx + {∫}_{- 3}^{0}\left|x + 5\right|dx$

$= - {∫}_{- 6}^{- 3}\left(x + 1\right)dx + {∫}_{- 3}^{0}\left(x + 5\right)dx$

$= - {\left[\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} + x\right]}_{- 6}^{- 3} + {\left[\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} + 5x\right]}_{- 3}^{0}$

$= - \left[\left(\dfrac{9}{2} - 3\right) - \left(18 - 6\right)\right] + \left[0 - \left(\dfrac{9}{2} - 15\right)\right]$

$= - \left[\dfrac{3}{2} - 12\right⌉ + \dfrac{21}{2} = \dfrac{21}{2} + \dfrac{21}{2} = 21$

questions.q: The value of the integral $\dfrac{48}{{\pi}^{4}}{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left(\dfrac{3\pi{x}^{2}}{2} - {x}^{3}\right)\dfrac{sinx}{1 + \cos^{2}x}dx$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Let $I = \dfrac{48}{{\pi}^{4}}{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}{x}^{2} - {x}^{3}\right)\dfrac{sinx}{1 + \cos^{2}x}dx \ldots \left(1\right)$

Using ${∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{a}^{b}f ( a + b - x ) dx$

We get $I = \dfrac{48}{{\pi}^{4}}{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}{\left(\pi - x\right)}^{2} - {\left(\pi - x\right)}^{3}\right)\dfrac{sin\left(0 + \pi - x\right)}{1 + \cos^{2}\left(0 + \pi - x\right)}dx$

$I = \dfrac{48}{{\pi}^{4}}{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left(\dfrac{3{\pi}^{3}}{2} - 3{\pi}^{2}x + \dfrac{3\pi{x}^{2}}{2} - {\pi}^{3} + {x}^{3} + 3{\pi}^{2}x - 3\pi{x}^{2}\right)\dfrac{sinx}{1 + \cos^{2}x}dx$ ..............equation $2$

Now adding equation (1) + equation (2)

$2I = \dfrac{48}{{\pi}^{4}}{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left(\dfrac{3{\pi}^{3}}{2} - {\pi}^{3}\right)\dfrac{sinx}{1 + \cos^{2}x}dx$

$2I = \dfrac{48}{{\pi}^{4}} \times \dfrac{{\pi}^{3}}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{sinx}{1 + \cos^{2}x}dx$

$2I = \dfrac{24}{\pi} \times 2 \times {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sinx}{1 + \cos^{2}x}dx$

Let $cosx = t ⇒ - sinxdx = dt$

So $I = \dfrac{24}{\pi} \times {∫}_{1}^{0}\dfrac{- dt}{1 + {t}^{2}}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{- 24}{\pi}{\left[\tan^{1}t\right]}_{1}^{0}$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{24}{\pi}\left[0 - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right] = 6$

questions.q: The value of $b > 3$ for which $12{∫}_{3}^{b}\dfrac{1}{\left({x}^{2} - 1\right)\left({x}^{2} - 4\right)}dx = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{49}{40}\right)$, is equal to _____.
questions.solution:
Given $12 \times {∫}_{3}^{b}\dfrac{1dx}{\left({x}^{2} - 4\right)\left({x}^{2} - 1\right)} = ln\left[\dfrac{49}{40}\right] \text{ and } 4b > 3$

$⇒$ By Using partial fraction

$\dfrac{1}{\left({x}^{2} - 4\right)\left({x}^{2} - 1\right)} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{1}{{x}^{2} - 4} - \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2} - 1}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{12}{3}{∫}_{3}^{b}\left[\dfrac{1}{{x}^{2} - 4} - \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2} - 1}\right] = ln\left(\dfrac{49}{40}\right)$

$⇒ 4{\left[\dfrac{1}{4}log\left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x + 2}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}log\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1}\right)\right]}_{3}^{b} = ln\left(\dfrac{49}{40}\right)$

$⇒ log\left(\dfrac{\left(b - 2\right){\left(b + 1\right)}^{2}}{\left(b + 2\right){\left(b - 1\right)}^{2}} \times \dfrac{5}{4}\right) = log\dfrac{49}{40}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(b - 2\right){\left(b + 1\right)}^{2}}{\left(b + 2\right){\left(b - 1\right)}^{2}} \times \dfrac{5}{4} = \dfrac{49}{40}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(b - 2\right){\left(b + 1\right)}^{2}}{\left(b + 2\right){\left(b - 1\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{49}{50} . . . \left(i\right)$

Comparing by hit and trial and taking ${\left(b + 1\right)}^{2} = 49 ⇒ b + 1 = 7 ⇒ b = 6$

Now putting $b = 6$ in equation (i) to corsscheck,

we get $\dfrac{4 \times {7}^{2}}{8 \times {5}^{2}} = \dfrac{49}{50}$ which is true

So $b = 6$ is correct option,

Hence $b = 6$

questions.q: The value of ${∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{{e}^{cosx}sinx}{\left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right)\left({e}^{cosx} + {e}^{- cosx}\right)}dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given $I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{sinx ⋅ {e}^{cosx}}{\left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right)\left({e}^{cosx} + {e}^{- cosx}\right)}dx . . . \left(i\right)$

Using property of integral $\mathop{∫ f}_{a}^{b}\left(a + b - x\right) = \mathop{∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)$

we get $I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{sinx ⋅ {e}^{- cosx}}{\left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right)\left({e}^{- cosx} + {e}^{cosx}\right)}dx . . . \left(ii\right)$

Adding equation $\left(i\right)$ & $\left(ii\right)$ we get

$2I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{sinx}{\left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right)} ⋅ \dfrac{\left({e}^{cosx} + {e}^{- cosx}\right)}{{e}^{cosx} + {e}^{- cosx}}dx$

$2I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{sinx}{1 + \cos^{2}x}dx$⇒ 2I = 2\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sinx}{1 + \cos^{2}x}dx$

Let $cosx = t ⇒ - sinxdx = dt$

$I = - \mathop{∫}_{1}^{0}\dfrac{dt}{1 + {t}^{2}} ⇒ I = - {\left[\tan^{- 1}t\right]}_{1}^{0} = - \left[0 - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right]$= \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Adding equation $\left(i\right)$ & $\left(ii\right)$ we get

$2I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{sinx}{\left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right)} ⋅ \dfrac{\left({e}^{cosx} + {e}^{- cosx}\right)}{{e}^{cosx} + {e}^{- cosx}}dx$

Let $cosx = t ⇒ - sinxdx = dt$

questions.q: The value of the integral${∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{dx}{\left(1 + {e}^{x}\right)\left(\sin^{6}x + \cos^{6}x\right)}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let, $I = {∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{dx}{\left(1 + {e}^{x}\right)\left({sm}^{6}x + \cos^{6}x\right)} . . . \left(i\right)$

Now we know ${∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right)dx$

$I = {∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{{e}^{x}dx}{\left(1 + {e}^{x}\right)\left(\sin^{6}x + \cos^{6}x\right)} . . . \left(ii\right)$

Adding $\left(i\right)$ and $\left(ii\right)$

$2I = {∫}_{\dfrac{- \pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\left(1 + {e}^{x}\right)dx}{\left(1 + {e}^{x}\right)\left(\sin^{6}x + \cos^{6}x\right)}$

$I = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{dx}{\left(\sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x\right)\left(\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x - \sin^{2}x\cos^{2}x\right)}$

$\mathop{= ∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{dx}{{\left(\sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x\right)}^{2} - 3\sin^{2}x\cos^{2}x} = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{dx}{1 - \dfrac{3}{4}\sin^{2}2x}$


$= {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{4{sec}^{2}2xdx}{4\left(1 + \tan^{2}2x\right) - 3\tan^{2}2x} = 2{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{4{sec}^{2}2x}{4 + \tan^{2}2x}dx$

Let $tan2x = t$ and $2{sec}^{2}2xdx = dt$

$I = 4\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\infty}\dfrac{dt}{{2}^{2} + {t}^{2}} = \dfrac{4}{2}{\left[\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{t}{2}\right]}_{0}^{\infty}$= 2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - 0\right) = \pi$
questions.question: The value of the integral${∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{dx}{\left(1 + {e}^{x}\right)\left(\sin^{6}x + \cos^{6}x\right)}$ is equal to
questions.explanation:
Let, $I = {∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{dx}{\left(1 + {e}^{x}\right)\left({sm}^{6}x + \cos^{6}x\right)} . . . \left(i\right)$

Now we know ${∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right)dx$

$I = {∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{{e}^{x}dx}{\left(1 + {e}^{x}\right)\left(\sin^{6}x + \cos^{6}x\right)} . . . \left(ii\right)$

Adding $\left(i\right)$ and $\left(ii\right)$

$2I = {∫}_{\dfrac{- \pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\left(1 + {e}^{x}\right)dx}{\left(1 + {e}^{x}\right)\left(\sin^{6}x + \cos^{6}x\right)}$

$I = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{dx}{\left(\sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x\right)\left(\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x - \sin^{2}x\cos^{2}x\right)}$

$\mathop{= ∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{dx}{{\left(\sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x\right)}^{2} - 3\sin^{2}x\cos^{2}x} = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{dx}{1 - \dfrac{3}{4}\sin^{2}2x}$


$= {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{4{sec}^{2}2xdx}{4\left(1 + \tan^{2}2x\right) - 3\tan^{2}2x} = 2{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{4{sec}^{2}2x}{4 + \tan^{2}2x}dx$

Let $tan2x = t$ and $2{sec}^{2}2xdx = dt$

$I = 4\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\infty}\dfrac{dt}{{2}^{2} + {t}^{2}} = \dfrac{4}{2}{\left[\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{t}{2}\right]}_{0}^{\infty}$= 2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - 0\right) = \pi$

questions.q:
$\lim_{n \to \infty}\left(\dfrac{{n}^{2}}{\left({n}^{2} + 1\right)\left(n + 1\right)} + \dfrac{{n}^{2}}{\left({n}^{2} + 4\right)\left(n + 2\right)} + \dfrac{{n}^{2}}{\left({n}^{2} + 9\right)\left(n + 3\right)} + \ldots + \dfrac{{n}^{2}}{\left({n}^{2} + {n}^{2}\right)\left(n + n\right)}\right)$
is equal to
questions.solution:
$\lim_{n \to \infty}\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{n}}{\left(1 + \dfrac{{r}^{2}}{{n}^{2}}\right)\left(1 + \dfrac{r}{n}\right)} = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{dx}{\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right)\left(1 + x\right)}$

Let $I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{dx}{\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right)\left(1 + x\right)}$

Now $x = tan\theta, dx = {sec}^{2}\thetad\theta$

$I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{d\theta}{1 + tan\theta} = \dfrac{1}{2}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{2cos\thetad\theta}{sin\theta + cos\theta}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{\left(sin\theta + cos\theta\right)d\theta}{sin\theta + cos\theta} + \dfrac{1}{2}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{\left(cos\theta - sin\theta\right)d\theta}{sin\theta + cos\theta}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{1}{2}{\left[ln\left|sin\theta + cos\theta\right|\right]}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}$= \dfrac{\pi}{8} + \dfrac{1}{4}ln2$

questions.q: Let $\mathop{Max}_{0 ⩽ x ⩽ 2}\left\{\dfrac{9 - {x}^{2}}{5 - x}\right\} = \alpha$ and $\mathop{Min}_{0 ⩽ x ⩽ 2}\left\{\dfrac{9 - {x}^{2}}{5 - x}\right\} = \beta$. If ${∫}_{\beta - \dfrac{8}{3}}^{2\alpha - 1} Max \left\{\dfrac{9 - {x}^{2}}{5 - x}, x\right\}dx = {\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}{\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{8}{15}\right)$, then ${\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}$ is equal to ______
questions.solution:
Here $y = \dfrac{9 - {x}^{2}}{5 - x} = 5 + x + \dfrac{16}{x - 5}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 - \dfrac{16}{{\left(x - 5\right)}^{2}}$

When $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0 ⇒ 1 - \dfrac{16}{{\left(x - 5\right)}^{2}} = 0$

So critical point is x = 1 in $\left[0, 2\right]$

Now we get $y\left(0\right) = \dfrac{9}{5}, y\left(1\right) = 2, y\left(2\right) = \dfrac{5}{3}$

So $\alpha = 2$ and $\beta = \dfrac{5}{3}$

$I = {∫}_{- 1}^{3}max\left(\dfrac{9 - {x}^{2}}{5 - x}, x\right)$

$I = {∫}_{- 1}^{\dfrac{9}{5}}\left(5 + x + \dfrac{16}{x - 5}\right)dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{9}{5}}^{3}xdx$

$= {\left[5x + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} + 16ln\left(x - 5\right)\right]}_{- 1}^{\dfrac{9}{5}} + {\left[\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right]}_{\dfrac{9}{5}}^{3}$

$I = 18 + 16ln\left(\dfrac{8}{15}\right)$

${\alpha}_{1} = 18$ and ${\alpha}_{2} = 16$

$⇒ {\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2} = 34$

questions.q: The function $f ( x ) ,$ that satisfies the condition $f ( x ) = x + {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}sinxcosyf ( y ) dy,$ is :
questions.solution:
Given the function $f\left(x\right) = x + {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}sinx \cdot cosyf\left(y\right)dy$

$f\left(x\right) = x + ksinx . . . \left(i\right)$

$f\left(y\right) = y + ksiny . . . \left(ii\right)

$k = {∫}_{0}^${\dfrac{\pi}{2}}$cosyf $\left(y\right)$dy$

From equations \left(i\right)\text{$ and }$\left(ii\right)

$f$\left(x\right)$ = x + {∫}_{0}^${\dfrac{\pi}{2}}$sinxcosy $\left(y + ksiny\right)$dy$

$f$\left(x\right)$ = x + sinx{∫}_{0}^${\dfrac{\pi}{2}}$ycosydy + $\dfrac{k}{2}$sinx{∫}_{0}^${\dfrac{\pi}{2}}$sin2ydy$

$f$\left(x\right)$ = x + sinx $\left[y{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}cosydy - {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left\{\dfrac{d}{dy}y{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}cosydy\right\}$dy\right] + $\dfrac{k}{2}$sinx{∫}_{0}^${\dfrac{\pi}{2}}$sin2ydy$

$f$\left(x\right)$ = x + sinx $\left[\dfrac{\pi}{2} -1\right]$ + $\dfrac{k}{2}$sinx \times $\left(1\right)$

$f\left(x\right) = x + \dfrac{( \pi - 2 ) sinx}{2} + \dfrac{ksinx}{2} . . . \left(iii\right)

from $( i ) and ( iii )$

$k = $\dfrac{\pi}{2} -$ 1 + $\dfrac{k}{2}

$k = \pi - 2$

Hence, $f ( x ) = x + ( \pi - 2 ) sinx$

$
