questions.q: If $\left[x\right]$ is the greatest integer $\le x,$ then ${\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{2}\left(sin\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right){\left(x - \left[x\right]\right)}^{[ x ]}dx$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Let, $I = {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right){\left(x - \left[x\right]\right)}^{[ x ]}dx$

$I = {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right){\left(x - \left[x\right]\right)}^{[ x ]}dx + {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{1}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right){\left(x - \left[x\right]\right)}^{[ x ]}dx$

$I = {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right){x}^{0}dx + {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{1}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right){\left(x - 1\right)}^{1}dx$

$I = {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)dx + {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{1}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\left(x - 1\right)dx$

$I = {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)dx + {\pi}^{2}\left[x{∫}_{1}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right) d x - {∫}_{1}^{2}\left\{\dfrac{d}{dx}x{∫}_{1}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)dx\right\}dx\right] - {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{1}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)dx$

$I = {\pi}^{2}{\left[- \dfrac{2}{\pi}cos\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\right]}_{0}^{1} + {\pi}^{2}{\left[\left(x\right)\dfrac{2}{\pi}\right \left(- cos\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\right)}_{1}^{2}\left- {∫}_{1}^{2}\dfrac{2}{\pi}\left(- cos\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)dx\right] + {\pi}^{2} \times \dfrac{2}{\pi}{\left[cos\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{2}\right)\right]}_{1}^{2}$

$I = {\pi}^{2}{\left[- \dfrac{2}{\pi}cos\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\right]}_{0}^{1} + {\pi}^{2}{\left[\left(x\right)\dfrac{2}{\pi}\right \left(- cos\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\right)}_{1}^{2}\left+ {\left(\dfrac{2}{\pi}\right)}^{2}{\left[sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{2}\right)\right]}_{1}^{2}\right] + {\pi}^{2} \times \dfrac{2}{\pi}{\left[cos\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{2}\right)\right]}_{1}^{2}$

$I = - {\pi}^{2}\left[\dfrac{2}{\pi}cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - \dfrac{2}{\pi}cos\left(0\right)\right] + {\pi}^{2}\left[2 \times \dfrac{2}{\pi}\left(- cos\pi\right) + 1 \times \dfrac{2}{\pi} \times \left(cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\right]\left+ 4\left[sin\left(\pi\right) - sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]\right] + {\pi}^{2} \times \dfrac{2}{\pi}\left[cos\left(\pi\right) - cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$

$I = 2\pi + 4\pi + 4 ( 0 - 1 ) - 2\pi$

$I = 4\pi - 4$

$I = 4\left(\pi - 1\right)$

questions.q: Let $f$ be a non-negative function in $[ 0, 1 ]$ and twice differentiable in $( 0, 1 ) .$ If ${∫}_{0}^{x}\sqrt{1 - {\left({f}^{'} ( t )\right)}^{2}}dt = {∫}_{0}^{x}f ( t ) dt, 0 \le x \le 1$ and $f ( 0 ) = 0,$ then $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}}{∫}_{0}^{x}f ( t ) dt:$
questions.solution:
Newton - Leibnitz rule

$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left({∫}_{f\left(x\right)}^{g\left(x\right)}h\left(x\right) d x\right) = g ' \left(x\right)h\left(g ( x )\right) - f ' \left(x\right)h\left(f ( x )\right)$

Given that

${∫}_{0}^{x}\sqrt{1 - {\left({f}^{'} ( t )\right)}^{2}}dt = {∫}_{0}^{x}f ( t ) dt$

Differentiate $w . r . t . x$

$\sqrt{1 - {\left({f}^{'} ( x )\right)}^{2}} = f ( x )$

Squaring on both sides
$⇒ 1 - {\left({f}^{'} ( x )\right)}^{2} = ( f ( x ) {)}^{2}$

$⇒ {\left({f}^{'} ( x )\right)}^{2} = 1 - ( f ( x ) {)}^{2}$

$f\left(x\right) = y ⇒ f ' \left(x\right) = \dfrac{dy}{dx}$
$⇒ {\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)}^{2} = 1 - {y}^{2} ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \pm \sqrt{1 - {y}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{\sqrt{1 - {y}^{2}}} = \pm dx$

By using Variable Separable form

$\sin^{- 1}y = \pm x + c$

When $x = 0, y = 0 ⇒ c = 0 .$

$∴ \sin^{- 1}y = x ⇒ y = sinx$

Now $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}}{∫}_{0}^{x}sintdt$

It is in the form of $\dfrac{0}{0}$ so apply L hospital's rule

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[{∫}_{0}^{x}sintdt\right]}{\dfrac{d \left({x}^{2}\right)}{d x}}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{sinx}{x}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.q: The value of the integral ${∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{\sqrt{x}dx}{( 1 + x ) ( 1 + 3x ) ( 3 + x )}$ is:
questions.solution:
Let $\sqrt{x} = t$

$⇒ x = {t}^{2}, dx = 2tdt$

Let $I = {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{\sqrt{x}dx}{( 1 + x ) ( 1 + 3x ) ( 3 + x )}$

$I = {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{2{t}^{2}dt}{\left({t}^{2} + 1\right)\left(3{t}^{2} + 1\right)\left({t}^{2} + 3\right)}$

$= {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{\left(\left(3{t}^{2} + 1\right) - \left({t}^{2} + 1\right)\right)dt}{\left({t}^{2} + 1\right)\left(3{t}^{2} + 1\right)\left({t}^{2} + 3\right)}$

$= {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\left({t}^{2} + 3\right)\left({t}^{2} + 1\right)} - \dfrac{1}{\left({t}^{2} + 3\right)\left(3{t}^{2} + 1\right)}\right)dt$

$= {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\dfrac{dt}{2\left({t}^{2} + 1\right)} - \dfrac{1}{8}\dfrac{3dt}{\left(3{t}^{2} + 1\right)} - \dfrac{3}{8}\dfrac{dt}{\left({t}^{2} + 3\right)}\right)$

$= {\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{- 1} ⁡ t - \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{8 \times 3}\tan^{- 1} ⁡ \sqrt{3}t - \dfrac{3}{8\sqrt{3}}\tan^{- 1} ⁡ \dfrac{t}{\sqrt{3}}\right)}_{0}^{1}$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{8} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{8} \times \dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{8} \times \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{8} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}\pi}{16}$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{8}\left(1 - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$

questions.solution:
${U}_{n} = \mathop{∏}_{r = 1}^{n}{\left(1 + \dfrac{{r}^{2}}{{n}^{2}}\right)}^{r}$

$L = \lim_{n \to \infty}\left({U}_{n}\right)\dfrac{- 4}{{n}^{2}}$

$logL = \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{- 4}{{n}^{2}}\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}log{\left(1 + \dfrac{{r}^{2}}{{n}^{2}}\right)}^{r}$

$logL = \lim_{n \to \infty}\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}\dfrac{- 4r}{n} \cdot \dfrac{1}{n}log\left(1 + \dfrac{{r}^{2}}{{n}^{2}}\right)$

$logL = - 4{∫}_{0}^{1}xlog\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right) d x$

Put $1 + {x}^{2} = t$

$2xdx = dt$

$= - 2{∫}_{1}^{2}log\left(t\right) d t = - 2{\left[tlogt - t\right]}_{1}^{2}$

$⇒ logL = - 2\left(2log2 - 1\right)$

$∴ L = {e}^{- 2\left(2log2 - 1\right)}$

$= {e}^{- 2\left(log\dfrac{4}{e}\right)} = {e}^{log{\left(\dfrac{4}{e}\right)}^{- 2}}$

$L = {\left(\dfrac{e}{4}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{{e}^{2}}{16}$

$= {∫}_{\dfrac{- 1}{\sqrt{2}}}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\sqrt{{\left(\dfrac{- 4x}{{x}^{2} - 1}\right)}^{2}}dx$

$= {∫}_{\dfrac{- 1}{\sqrt{2}}}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\sqrt{{\left(\dfrac{4x}{1 - {x}^{2}}\right)}^{2}}dx$

$= {∫}_{\dfrac{- 1}{\sqrt{2}}}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\sqrt{\dfrac{16{x}^{2}}{{\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)}^{2}}}dx$

$= {∫}_{\dfrac{- 1}{\sqrt{2}}}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\left\{\dfrac{4\left|x\right|}{\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)}\right\}dx$

$= \dfrac{3}{2}{∫}_{- 1}^{0}\dfrac{{e}^{\alpha}d\alpha}{\sqrt{1 + \alpha}} - 1\left(Put - \sin^{2}x = \alpha\right)$

$= \dfrac{3}{2e}{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{{e}^{x}}{\sqrt{x}}dx - 1\left(Put1 + \alpha = x\right)$

$= \dfrac{3}{2e}{∫}_{0}^{1}{e}^{x}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}dx - 1 = \dfrac{3}{2e}\left({\left(2\sqrt{x}{e}^{x}\right)}_{0}^{1} - {∫}_{0}^{1}2\sqrt{x}{e}^{x}dx\right) - 1$

$= \dfrac{3}{2e}\left(\left(2e\right) - {∫}_{0}^{1}2\sqrt{x}{e}^{x}dx\right) - 1$

$= 2 - \dfrac{3}{e}{∫}_{0}^{1}{e}^{x}\sqrt{x}dx$

Hence, $\alpha + \beta = 5 .$

questions.solution:
$I = {∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{dx}{\left(1 + {e}^{xcosx}\right)\left(\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x\right)} \ldots \left(1\right)$

Using ${∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right)dx$

$I = {∫}_{- \pi / 4}^{\pi / 4}\dfrac{dx}{\left(1 + {e}^{- xcosx}\right)\left(\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x\right)} . . . \left(2\right)$

Add $\left(1\right)$ and $\left(2\right)$

$2I = {∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{dx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}$

$⇒ 2I = 2{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{dx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{\left(1 + \tan^{2}x\right){sec}^{2}x}{\tan^{4}x + 1}dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{\tan^{2}x}\right){sec}^{2}x}{{\left(tanx - \dfrac{1}{tanx}\right)}^{2} + 2}dx$

Put $tanx - \dfrac{1}{tanx} = t$

$⇒ \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{\tan^{2}x}\right){sec}^{2}xdx = dt$

So, $I = {∫}_{- \infty}^{0}\dfrac{dt}{{t}^{2} + 2} = {\left[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{t}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\right]}_{- \infty}^{0}$

$⇒ I = 0 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(- \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2\sqrt{2}}$

questions.q: Let $F: \left[3, 5\right] \to R$ be a twice differentiable function on $\left(3, 5\right)$ such that $F\left(x\right) = {e}^{- x}{∫}_{3}^{x}\left(3{t}^{2} + 2t + 4{F}^{'}\left(t\right)\right)dt .$ If ${F}^{'}\left(4\right) = \dfrac{\alpha{e}^{\beta} - 224}{{\left({e}^{\beta} - 4\right)}^{2}}$, then $\alpha + \beta$ is equal to _____.
questions.solution:
Given,

$F\left(x\right) = {e}^{- x}{∫}_{3}^{x}\left(3{t}^{2} + 2t + 4{F}^{'}\left(t\right)\right)dt .$

So, $F\left(3\right) = {e}^{- 3}{∫}_{3}^{3}\left(3{t}^{2} + 2t + 4{F}^{'}\left(t\right)\right)dt .$

$⇒ F\left(3\right) = 0$

Again, ${e}^{x}F\left(x\right) = {∫}_{3}^{x}\left(3{t}^{2} + 2t + 4{F}^{'}\left(t\right)\right)dt$

Differentiate both sides

$⇒ {e}^{x}F\left(x\right) + {e}^{x}{F}^{'}\left(x\right) = 3{x}^{2} + 2x + 4{F}^{'}\left(x\right)$ (Newton Leibnitz Theorem for Definite Integral)

$⇒ \left({e}^{x} - 4\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + {e}^{x}y = \left(3{x}^{2} + 2x\right)$ (Use $y = F\left(x\right)$)

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{{e}^{x}}{\left({e}^{x} - 4\right)}y = \dfrac{\left(3{x}^{2} + 2x\right)}{\left({e}^{x} - 4\right)}$

Here, integrating factor is ${e}^{∫ \dfrac{{e}^{x}}{{e}^{x} - 4}dx} = {e}^{ln\left({e}^{x} - 4\right)} = {e}^{x} - 4$

So, the solution is

$y \cdot \left({e}^{x} - 4\right) = ∫ \left(3{x}^{2} + 2x\right)dx + c$

$⇒ y \cdot \left({e}^{x} - 4\right) = \left({x}^{3} + {x}^{2}\right) + c$

Put $x = 3, y = 0 ⇒ c = - 36$

So, $F\left(x\right) = \dfrac{\left({x}^{3} + {x}^{2} - 36\right)}{\left({e}^{x} - 4\right)}$

$⇒ {F}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{\left(3{x}^{2} + 2x\right)\left({e}^{x} - 4\right) - \left({x}^{3} + {x}^{2} - 36\right){e}^{x}}{{\left({e}^{x} - 4\right)}^{2}}$

Now put value of $x = 4$ we will get

${F}^{'}\left(4\right) = \dfrac{\left(3{\left(4\right)}^{2} + 2\left(4\right)\right)\left({e}^{4} - 4\right) - \left({\left(4\right)}^{3} + {\left(4\right)}^{2} - 36\right){e}^{4}}{{\left({e}^{4} - 4\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{12{e}^{4} - 224}{{\left({e}^{4} - 4\right)}^{2}}$

So, $\alpha = 12 \text{ and } \beta = 4$

Hence, $\alpha + \beta = 16$

questions.q: The value of the integral ${∫}_{- 1}^{1}log\left(x + \sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1}\right)dx$ is:
questions.solution:
Let $I = {∫}_{- 1}^{1}log\left(x + \sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1}\right)dx$

Consider $f\left(x\right) = log\left(x + \sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1}\right)$

Now, $f\left(- x\right) = log\left(- x + \sqrt{1 + {x}^{2}}\right)$

$⇒ f\left(- x\right) = - log\left(x + \sqrt{1 + {x}^{2}}\right)$

$⇒ f\left(- x\right) = - f\left(x\right)$

So, $f\left(x\right)$ is an odd function.

$∴ I = 0$

questions.q: If ${∫}_{0}^{100\pi}\dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{{e}^{\left(\dfrac{x}{\pi} - \left[\dfrac{x}{\pi}\right]\right)}}dx = \dfrac{\alpha{\pi}^{3}}{1 + 4{\pi}^{2}}, \alpha \in R$ where $\left[x\right]$ is the greatest integer less than or equal to $x,$ then the value of $\alpha$ is:
questions.solution:
Let, $I = {∫}_{0}^{100\pi}\dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{{e}^{\left(\dfrac{x}{\pi} - \left[\dfrac{x}{\pi}\right]\right)}}dx$

We know that if $f\left(x\right)$ is a periodic function, with period $T$ then ${∫}_{0}^{nT}f\left(x\right)dx = n{∫}_{0}^{T}f\left(x\right)dx, n \in Z$

$⇒ I = 100{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{{e}^{\left(\dfrac{x}{\pi} - \left[\dfrac{x}{\pi}\right]\right)}}dx$

For, $0 < x < \pi, 0 < \dfrac{x}{\pi} < 1$⇒ \left[\dfrac{x}{\pi}\right] = 0$

$⇒ I = 100{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{{e}^{\left(\dfrac{x}{\pi}\right)}}dx$

Now, using $cos2x = 1 - 2\sin^{2}x,$ we get

$I = 100{∫}_{0}^{\pi}{e}^{- x / \pi}\dfrac{\left(1 - cos2x\right)}{2}dx$

$⇒ I = 100 \times \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left({e}^{- x / \pi} - {e}^{- x / \pi} \cdot cos2x\right)dx$

$⇒ I = 50\left\{{∫}_{0}^{\pi}{e}^{- x / \pi}dx - {∫}_{0}^{\pi}{e}^{- x / \pi} \cdot cos2xdx\right\}$

Let, ${I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}{e}^{- x / \pi}dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {\left[- \pi{e}^{- x / \pi}\right]}_{0}^{\pi}$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = - \pi\left({e}^{- \pi / \pi} - {e}^{0}\right) = \pi\left(1 - {e}^{- 1}\right)$

And, let ${I}_{2} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}{e}^{- x / \pi} \cdot cos2xdx$

By using $ILATE$ rule,

${I}_{2} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}cos2x \cdot {e}^{- x / \pi}dx$

Now, using integration by parts, i.e. $∫ \left(u \cdot v\right)dx = u ∫ vdx - ∫ \left[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(u\right) ∫ vdx\right]dx,$ we get

$⇒ {I}_{2} = - \pi{\left[{e}^{- x / \pi} \cdot cos2x\right]}_{0}^{\pi} - {∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left(- \pi{e}^{- x / \pi} \cdot \left(- 2sin2x\right)\right)dx$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = \pi\left(1 - {e}^{- 1}\right) - 2\pi{∫}_{0}^{\pi}{e}^{- x / \pi}sin2xdx$

Again, applying integration by parts, we get

$\left{I}_{2} = \pi\left(1 - {e}^{- 1}\right) - 2\pi { {\left[- \pi{e}^{- x / \pi}sin2x\right]}_{0}^{\pi} - {∫}_{0}^{\pi} - \pi{e}^{- x / \pi}2cos2xdx\right\}$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = \pi\left(1 - {e}^{- 1}\right) - 4{\pi}^{2}{I}_{2}$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = \dfrac{\pi\left(1 - {e}^{- 1}\right)}{1 + 4{\pi}^{2}}$

$∴ I = 50\left({I}_{1} + {I}_{2}\right)$

$⇒ I = 50\left\{\pi\left(1 - {e}^{- 1}\right) - \dfrac{\pi\left(1 - {e}^{- 1}\right)}{1 + 4{\pi}^{2}}\right\}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{200\left(1 - {e}^{- 1}\right){\pi}^{3}}{1 + 4{\pi}^{2}}$

Given $I = \dfrac{\alpha{\pi}^{3}}{1 + 4{\pi}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\alpha{\pi}^{3}}{1 + 4{\pi}^{2}} = \dfrac{200\left(1 - {e}^{- 1}\right){\pi}^{3}}{1 + 4{\pi}^{2}}$

$⇒ \alpha = 200\left(1 - {e}^{- 1}\right) .$

$⇒ I = 50\left\{{∫}_{0}^{\pi}{e}^{- x / \pi}dx - {∫}_{0}^{\pi}{e}^{- x / \pi} \cdot cos2xdx\right\}$

Let, ${I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}{e}^{- x / \pi}dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {\left[- \pi{e}^{- x / \pi}\right]}_{0}^{\pi}$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = - \pi\left({e}^{- \pi / \pi} - {e}^{0}\right) = \pi\left(1 - {e}^{- 1}\right)$

And, let ${I}_{2} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}{e}^{- x / \pi} \cdot cos2xdx$

By using $ILATE$ rule,

${I}_{2} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}cos2x \cdot {e}^{- x / \pi}dx$

Now, using integration by parts, i.e. $∫ \left(u \cdot v\right)dx = u ∫ vdx - ∫ \left[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(u\right) ∫ vdx\right]dx,$ we get

$⇒ {I}_{2} = - \pi{\left[{e}^{- x / \pi} \cdot cos2x\right]}_{0}^{\pi} - {∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left(- \pi{e}^{- x / \pi} \cdot \left(- 2sin2x\right)\right)dx$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = \pi\left(1 - {e}^{- 1}\right) - 2\pi{∫}_{0}^{\pi}{e}^{- x / \pi}sin2xdx$

Again, applying integration by parts, we get

$\left{I}_{2} = \pi\left(1 - {e}^{- 1}\right) - 2\pi { {\left[- \pi{e}^{- x / \pi}sin2x\right]}_{0}^{\pi} - {∫}_{0}^{\pi} - \pi{e}^{- x / \pi}2cos2xdx\right\}$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = \pi\left(1 - {e}^{- 1}\right) - 4{\pi}^{2}{I}_{2}$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = \dfrac{\pi\left(1 - {e}^{- 1}\right)}{1 + 4{\pi}^{2}}$

$∴ I = 50\left({I}_{1} + {I}_{2}\right)$

$⇒ I = 50\left\{\pi\left(1 - {e}^{- 1}\right) - \dfrac{\pi\left(1 - {e}^{- 1}\right)}{1 + 4{\pi}^{2}}\right\}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{200\left(1 - {e}^{- 1}\right){\pi}^{3}}{1 + 4{\pi}^{2}}$

Given $I = \dfrac{\alpha{\pi}^{3}}{1 + 4{\pi}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\alpha{\pi}^{3}}{1 + 4{\pi}^{2}} = \dfrac{200\left(1 - {e}^{- 1}\right){\pi}^{3}}{1 + 4{\pi}^{2}}$

$⇒ \alpha = 200\left(1 - {e}^{- 1}\right) .$

questions.q: If $[ x ]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $x,$ then the value of the integral ${∫}_{- \pi / 2}^{\pi / 2}\left[\left[x\right] - sinx\right]dx$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
We have,

$I = {∫}_{- \pi / 2}^{\pi / 2}\left(\left[\left[x\right] - sinx\right]\right)dx \ldots \left(i\right)$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{- 1}\left(\left[\left[x\right] - sinx\right]\right)dx + {∫}_{- 1}^{0}\left(\left[\left[x\right] - sinx\right]\right)dx + {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\left[\left[x\right] - sinx\right]\right)dx + {∫}_{1}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(\left[\left[x\right] - sinx\right]\right)dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{- \pi / 2}^{- 1}\left(\left[- 2 - sinx\right]\right)dx + {∫}_{- 1}^{0}\left(\left[- 1 - sinx\right]\right)dx + {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\left[0 - sinx\right]\right)dx + {∫}_{1}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(\left[1 - sinx\right]\right)dx$

$⇒ I = - 2{∫}_{- \pi / 2}^{- 1}dx - {∫}_{- 1}^{0}dx - 1{∫}_{0}^{1}dx + {∫}_{1}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}0 \cdot dx$

$⇒ I = - 2\left(- 1 + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - 1 - 1$

$⇒ I = - \pi$

questions.q: If $f: R \to R$ is given by $f ( x ) = x + 1,$ then the value of $\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{1}{n}\left[f\left(0\right) + f\left(\dfrac{5}{n}\right) + f\left(\dfrac{10}{n}\right) + \ldots . . + f\left(\dfrac{5 ( n - 1 )}{n}\right)\right]$ is:
questions.solution:
Let

$I = \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{1}{n}\left[f\left(0\right) + f\left(\dfrac{5}{n}\right) + f\left(\dfrac{10}{n}\right) + \ldots . . + f\left(\dfrac{5 ( n - 1 )}{n}\right)\right]$

$⇒ I = \mathop{∑}_{r = 0}^{n - 1}f\left(\dfrac{5r}{n}\right)\dfrac{1}{n}$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{1}f\left(5x\right)dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(5x + 1\right)dx$

$⇒ I = {\left[\dfrac{5{x}^{2}}{2} + x\right]}_{0}^{1}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{5}{2} + 1 = \dfrac{7}{2}$

questions.q: Let $g\left(t\right) = {∫}_{- \pi / 2}^{\pi / 2}\left(cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}t + f\left(x\right)\right)dx,$ where $f\left(x\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(x + \sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1}\right), x \in R .$ Then which one of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
We have,

$f\left(x\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(x + \sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1}\right), x \in R$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{\left(x + \sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1}\right)\left(x - \sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1}\right)}{x - \sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1}}\right)$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{- 1}{x - \sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1}}\right)$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1} - x}\right)$

$⇒ f\left(- x\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1} + x}\right)$

$⇒ f\left(- x\right) = {\log}_{e}{\left(\sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1} + x\right)}^{- 1}$

$⇒ f\left(- x\right) = - {\log}_{e}\left(\sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1} + x\right)$

$⇒ f\left(- x\right) = - f\left(x\right)$

Hence, $f\left(x\right)$ is an odd function.

Now,

$g\left(t\right) = {∫}_{- \pi / 2}^{\pi / 2}\left(cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}t + f\left(x\right)\right)dx$

$⇒ g\left(t\right) = cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}t{∫}_{- \pi / 2}^{\pi / 2}1dx + {∫}_{- \pi / 2}^{\pi / 2}f\left(x\right)dx$

$⇒ g\left(t\right) = \picos\dfrac{\pi}{4}t + {∫}_{- \pi / 2}^{\pi / 2}f\left(x\right)dx$

$⇒ g\left(t\right) = \picos\dfrac{\pi}{4}t + 0$

$∵ f\left(x\right)$ is an odd function.

$∴ g\left(1\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{\sqrt{2}} ⇒ \sqrt{2}g\left(1\right) = \pi$

$g\left(0\right) = \pi$

questions.q: The value of the integral ${∫}_{- 1}^{1}{\log}_{e}\left(\sqrt{1 - x} + \sqrt{1 + x}\right)dx$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Let

$I = {∫}_{- 1}^{1}{\log}_{e}\left(\sqrt{1 - x} + \sqrt{1 + x}\right)dx$

$⇒ I = 2{∫}_{0}^{1}\mathop{\mathop{{\log}_{e}\left(\sqrt{1 - x} + \sqrt{1 + x}\right)}_{⏟}}_{I} \cdot \mathop{\mathop{1}_{⏟}}_{II}dx$

$⇒ I = 2\left[{\left(x{\log}_{e}\left(\sqrt{1 - x} + \sqrt{1 + x}\right)\right)}_{0}^{1} - {∫}_{0}^{1}x \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x} + \sqrt{1 + x}}\right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{1 + x}} - \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{1 - x}}\right)dx\right]$

$⇒ I = 2{\log}_{e}\sqrt{2} - \dfrac{2}{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\left\{\dfrac{x\left(\sqrt{1 - x} - \sqrt{1 + x}\right)}{\left(\sqrt{1 - x} + \sqrt{1 + x}\right)\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}\right\}dx$

$⇒ I = 2{\log}_{e}\sqrt{2} - {∫}_{0}^{1}\left\{\dfrac{x{\left(\sqrt{1 - x} - \sqrt{1 + x}\right)}^{2}}{- 2x\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}\right\}dx$

$⇒ I = \left({\log}_{e}2\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{\left(2 - 2\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}\right)}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}dx$

$⇒ I = \left({\log}_{e}2\right) + {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\dfrac{1 - \sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}\right)dx$

$⇒ I = \left({\log}_{e}2\right) + {\left(\sin^{- 1}x - x\right)}_{0}^{1}$

$⇒ I = \left({\log}_{e}2\right) + \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 1$

The largest possible interval in which $g ( 3 )$ lies is :
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{1}{3} \le f\left(t\right) \le 1 ∀ t \in \left[0, 1\right]$

$0 \le f\left(t\right) \le \dfrac{1}{2} ∀ t \in ( 1, 3 ]$

Now, $g\left(3\right) = {∫}_{0}^{3}f\left(t\right)dt = {∫}_{0}^{1}f\left(t\right)dt + {∫}_{1}^{3}f\left(t\right)dt$

$∵ {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{3}dt \le {∫}_{0}^{1}f\left(t\right)dt \le {∫}_{0}^{1}1 . dt . . . \left(1\right)$

and ${∫}_{1}^{3}0dt \le {∫}_{1}^{3}f\left(1\right)dt \le {∫}_{1}^{3}\dfrac{1}{2}dt . . . \left(2\right)$

Adding, we get

$\dfrac{1}{3} + 0 \le g\left(3\right) \le 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(3 - 1\right)$

$\dfrac{1}{3} \le g\left(3\right) \le 2$

questions.q: Let $f: R \to R$ be defined as $f\left(x\right) = {e}^{- x}sinx .$ If $F: \left[0, 1\right] \to R$ is a differentiable function such that $F\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}f\left(t\right)dt,$ then the value of ${∫}_{0}^{1}\left({F}^{'} ( x ) + f ( x )\right){e}^{x}dx$ lies in the interval
questions.solution:
Given $f ( x ) = {e}^{- x}sinx$

Now, $F\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}f\left(t\right)dt$

Using Newton Leibnitz rule i.e. $\dfrac{d}{dx}{∫}_{u\left(x\right)}^{v\left(x\right)}f\left(t\right)dt = f\left(v\left(x\right)\right) \cdot \left({v}^{'}\left(x\right)\right) - f\left(u\left(x\right)\right) \cdot \left({u}^{'}\left(x\right)\right),$

$⇒ {F}^{'} ( x ) = f ( x )$

Now, $I = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left({F}^{'} ( x ) + f ( x )\right){e}^{x}dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{1} ( f ( x ) + f ( x ) ) \cdot {e}^{x}dx$

$⇒ I = 2{∫}_{0}^{1}f ( x ) \cdot {e}^{x}dx$

$⇒ I = 2{∫}_{0}^{1}{e}^{- x}sinx \cdot {e}^{x}dx$

$⇒ I = 2{∫}_{0}^{1}sinxdx$

$⇒ I = 2{\left[- cosx\right]}_{0}^{1}$

Using the expansion of $cosx = 1 - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2 !} + \dfrac{{x}^{4}}{4 !} - \dfrac{{x}^{6}}{6 !} + . . .$

$⇒ I = 2\left\{1 - \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{4 !} + \dfrac{1}{6 !} + . . .\right)\right\}$

$⇒ I = 1 - \dfrac{2}{4 !} + \dfrac{2}{6 !} - \dfrac{2}{9 !} . . .$

$⇒ 1 - \dfrac{2}{4 !} < I < 1 - \dfrac{2}{4 !} + \dfrac{2}{6 !}$

$⇒ \dfrac{11}{12} < I < \dfrac{331}{360}$

$⇒ I \in \left[\dfrac{11}{12}, \dfrac{331}{360}\right]$

$⇒ I \in \left[\dfrac{330}{360}, \dfrac{331}{360}\right] .$

questions.q: If the integral ${∫}_{0}^{10}\dfrac{\left[sin2\pix\right]}{{e}^{x - \left[x\right]}}dx = \alpha{e}^{- 1} + \beta{e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}} + \gamma,$ where $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are integers and $\left[x\right]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $x,$ then the value of $\alpha + \beta + \gamma$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Let $I = {∫}_{0}^{10}\dfrac{\left[sin2\pix\right]}{{e}^{x - \left[x\right]}}dx = {∫}_{0}^{10}\dfrac{\left[sin2\pix\right]}{{e}^{\left\{x\right\}}}dx,$ where $x - \left[x\right] = \left\{x\right\}$ is the fractional part function.

We know that the $\left\{x\right\}$ is a periodic function with period $1$ and also that $sin2\pix$ is a periodic function with period $\dfrac{2\pi}{2\pi} = 1 .$

Thus, the function $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{\left[sin2\pix\right]}{{e}^{\left\{x\right\}}}$ is periodic with period $1 .$

If $f\left(x\right)$ is a periodic function with period $T$ then ${∫}_{0}^{nT}f\left(x\right)dx = n{∫}_{0}^{T}f\left(x\right)dx, n \in N$

Therefore $I = 10{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{\left[sin2\pix\right]}{{e}^{\left\{x\right\}}}dx$

$⇒ I = 10{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{\left[sin2\pix\right]}{{e}^{x}}dx$

Now, for $0 \le x \le 1 ⇒ - 1 \le sin2\pi x \le 1,$ hence $\left[sin2x\right]$ can take values $0$ and $- 1$

$⇒ I = 10\left({∫}_{0}^{1 / 2}\dfrac{\left[sin2\pix\right]}{{e}^{x}}dx + {∫}_{1 / 2}^{1}\dfrac{\left[sin2\pix\right]}{{e}^{x}}dx\right)$

$⇒ I = 10\left(0 + {∫}_{1 / 2}^{1}\dfrac{( - 1 )}{{e}^{x}}dx\right)$

$⇒ I = - 10{∫}_{1 / 2}^{1}{e}^{- x}dx$

$⇒ I = 10{\left[{e}^{- x}\right]}_{1 / 2}^{1}$

$⇒ I = 10\left({e}^{- 1} - {e}^{- 1 / 2}\right)$

Given, $I = \alpha{e}^{- 1} + \beta{e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}} + \gamma,$ thus $\alpha = 10, \beta = - 10, \gamma = 0 .$

And, $\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 10 - 10 = 0 .$

questions.q: Let ${I}_{n} = {∫}_{1}^{e}{x}^{19} ( log | x | {)}^{n}dx,$ where $n \in N$. If  $\left(20\right){I}_{10} = \alpha{I}_{9} + \beta{I}_{8},$ for natural numbers $\alpha and \beta$, then $\alpha - \beta$ equal to _______.
questions.solution:
Given ${I}_{n} = {∫}_{1}^{e}{x}^{19} ( log | x | {)}^{n}dx, n \in N$

$⇒ {I}_{n} = {∫}_{1}^{e}{x}^{19}{\left(logx\right)}^{n}dx, ∵$ for $1 0$

Integrating by using by parts rule, ${∫}_{a}^{b}\left(u \cdot v\right)dx = {\left[u ∫ vdx\right]}_{a}^{b} - {∫}_{a}^{b}\left[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(u\right) ∫ vdx\right]dx,$ taking $u = logx \text{ and } v = {x}^{19},$ we get

${I}_{n} = {\left[{\left(logx\right)}^{n} ∫ {x}^{19}dx\right]}_{1}^{e} - {∫}_{1}^{e}\left[\dfrac{d}{dx}{\left(logx\right)}^{n} ∫ {x}^{19}dx\right]dx$

$⇒ {I}_{n} = {\left[{\left(logx\right)}^{n}\left(\dfrac{{x}^{20}}{20}\right)\right]}_{1}^{e} - {∫}_{1}^{e}\left[n{\left(logx\right)}^{n - 1} \times \dfrac{1}{x} \times \left(\dfrac{{x}^{20}}{20}\right)\right]dx$

$⇒ {I}_{n} = \left[{\left(loge\right)}^{n}\left(\dfrac{{e}^{20}}{20}\right) - 0\right] - {∫}_{1}^{e}\left[n{\left(logx\right)}^{n - 1} \times \left(\dfrac{{x}^{19}}{20}\right)\right]dx$

$⇒ {I}_{n} = \left(\dfrac{{e}^{20}}{20}\right) - \dfrac{n}{20}{∫}_{1}^{e}{x}^{19}{\left(logx\right)}^{n - 1}dx$

$⇒ 20{I}_{n} = {e}^{20} - n{I}_{n - 1}$

Hence, we get $20{I}_{10} = {e}^{20} - 10{I}_{9} . . . \left(i\right)$ and

$20{I}_{9} = {e}^{20} - 9{I}_{8} . . . \left(ii\right)$

On subtracting the above two equations, we get

$20{I}_{10} - 20{I}_{9} = - 10{I}_{9} + 9{I}_{8}$

$⇒ 20{I}_{10} = 10{I}_{9} + 9{I}_{8}$

Given $20{I}_{10} = \alpha{I}_{9} + \beta{I}_{8}$

$⇒ \alpha = 10, \beta = 9$ and hence $\alpha - \beta = 1 .$

questions.q: Which of the following statement is correct for the function $g ( \alpha )$ for $\alpha \in R$ such that $g\left(\alpha\right) = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}\dfrac{\sin^{\alpha}x}{\cos^{\alpha}x + \sin^{\alpha}x}dx$
questions.solution:
$g\left(\alpha\right) = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}\dfrac{\sin^{\alpha}x}{\left(\sin^{\alpha}x + \cos^{\alpha}x\right)}dx \ldots \left(i\right)$

$g\left(\alpha\right) = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}\dfrac{\cos^{\alpha}x}{\left(\sin^{\alpha}x + \cos^{\alpha}x\right)}dx \ldots \left(ii\right)$

Adding $\left(1\right) + \left(2\right)$

$2g\left(\alpha\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$⇒ g\left(\alpha\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{12}$

Which is constant and an even function.

questions.q: If $[ \cdot ]$ represents the greatest integer function, then the value of $\left|{∫}_{0}^{\sqrt{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}}\left[\left[{x}^{2}\right] - cosx\right]dx\right|$ is ___________.
questions.solution:
$I = {∫}_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi / 2}}\left(\left[{x}^{2}\right] + \left[- cosx\right]\right)dx$

$= {∫}_{0}^{1}0dx + {∫}_{1}^{\sqrt{\pi / 2}}dx + {∫}_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi / 2}}\left(- 1\right)dx$

$= \sqrt{\dfrac{\pi}{2}} - 1 - \sqrt{\dfrac{\pi}{2}} = - 1$

$⇒ \left|I\right| = 1$

questions.solution:
${∫}_{0}^{1}\left({x}^{2} + bx + c\right)dx = 1$

$\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{b}{2} + c = 1 ⇒ \dfrac{b}{2} + c = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$3b + 6c = 4 . . . \left(1\right)$

$P\left(2\right) = 5$

$4 + 2b + c = 5$

$2b + c = 1 . . . \left(2\right)$

From $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$

$b = \dfrac{2}{9} \text{ and } c = \dfrac{5}{9}$

$9\left(b + c\right) = 7$

Let $f: \left(0, 2\right) \to R$ be defined as $f\left(x\right) = {\log}_{2}\left(1 + tan\left(\dfrac{\pix}{4}\right)\right)$.

Then, $\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{2}{n}\left(f\left(\dfrac{1}{n}\right) + f\left(\dfrac{2}{n}\right) + \ldots . + f\left(1\right)\right)$ is equal to ________.
questions.solution:
Given $f\left(x\right) = {\log}_{2}\left(1 + tan\left(\dfrac{\pix}{4}\right)\right) = \dfrac{{\log}_{e}\left(1 + tan\left(\dfrac{\pix}{4}\right)\right)}{{\log}_{e}2}$

$E = 2\lim_{n \to \infty}\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}\dfrac{1}{n}f\left(\dfrac{r}{n}\right)$

$E = \dfrac{2}{{\log}_{e}2}{∫}_{0}^{1}{\log}_{e}\left(1 + tan\dfrac{\pix}{4}\right)dx$. . . ( i )$

Replacing $x \to 1 - x$

$E = \dfrac{2}{{\log}_{e}2}{∫}_{0}^{1}{\log}_{e}\left(1 + tan\dfrac{\pi}{4}\left(1 - x\right)\right)dx$

$E = \dfrac{2}{{\log}_{e}2}{∫}_{0}^{1}{\log}_{e}\left(1 + tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}x\right)\right)dx$

$E = \dfrac{2}{{\log}_{e}2}{∫}_{0}^{1}{\log}_{e}\left(1 + \dfrac{1 - tan\dfrac{\pi}{4}x}{1 + tan\dfrac{\pi}{4}x}\right)dx$

$E = \dfrac{2}{{\log}_{e}2}{∫}_{0}^{1}{\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{2}{1 + tan\dfrac{\pix}{4}}\right)dx$

$E = \dfrac{2}{{\log}_{e}2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\left({\log}_{e}2 - {\log}_{e}\left(1 + tan\dfrac{\pix}{4}\right)\right)dx$. . . ( ii )$

Adding an equation $( i ) \text{ and } ( ii )$ we get,

$E = 1$

questions.q: Let $f: R \to R$ be a continuous function such that $f\left(x\right) + f\left(x + 1\right) = 2$ for all $x \in R$. If ${I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{8}f\left(x\right)dx$ and ${I}_{2} = {∫}_{- 1}^{3}f\left(x\right)dx$, then the value of ${I}_{1} + 2{I}_{2}$ is equal to ________.
questions.solution:
$f\left(x\right) + f\left(x + 1\right) = 2$

Replace $x\text{by}x + 1$

$f\left(x + 1\right) + f\left(x + 2\right) = 2$

By subtracting the equations, we get

$f\left(x\right) = f\left(x + 2\right)$

$⇒ f\left(x\right)$ is periodic with period $= 2$

${I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{8}f\left(x\right)dx = 4{∫}_{0}^{2}f\left(x\right)dx$

$= 4{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(f\left(x\right) + f\left(1 + x\right)\right)dx = 8$

Similarly, ${I}_{2} = 2 \times 2 = 4$

Hence, ${I}_{1} + 2{I}_{2} = 16$

$= 4{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(f\left(x\right) + f\left(1 + x\right)\right)dx = 8$

Similarly, ${I}_{2} = 2 \times 2 = 4$

Hence, ${I}_{1} + 2{I}_{2} = 16$

questions.q: For $x > 0$, if $f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{{\log}_{e}t}{\left(1 + t\right)}dt$, then $f\left(e\right) + f\left(\dfrac{1}{e}\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{{\log}_{e}t}{\left(1 + t\right)}dt$

$f\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) = {∫}_{1}^{1 / x}\dfrac{ℓnt}{1 + t}dt$, let $t = \dfrac{1}{y}$

$= {∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{ℓn\left(1 / y\right)}{1 + \left(1 / y\right)} . \left(\dfrac{- 1}{{y}^{2}}\right)dy$

$= + {∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{ℓny}{1 + y} . \dfrac{y}{{y}^{2}}dy$

$= {∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{ℓny}{y\left(1 + y\right)}dy$

hence

$f\left(x\right) + f\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) = {∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{\left(1 + t\right)ℓnt}{t\left(1 + t\right)}dt = {∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{ℓnt}{t}dt$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\ln^{2}\left(x\right)$

so $f\left(e\right) + f\left(\dfrac{1}{e}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2} . . . \left(3\right)$

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}{e}^{t}f\left(t\right)dt + {e}^{x}$ be a differentiable function for all $x \in R$. Then $f\left(x\right)$ equals :
questions.solution:
Given $f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}{e}^{t}f\left(t\right)dt + {e}^{x} ⇒ f\left(0\right) = 1$

Differentiating with respect to $x$ we get,

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = {e}^{x}f\left(x\right) + {e}^{x}$

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = {e}^{x}\left(f\left(x\right) + 1\right)$

$\dfrac{{f}^{'}\left(x\right)}{f\left(x\right) + 1} = {e}^{x}$

Integrate both the sides we get,

${∫}_{0}^{x}\dfrac{{f}^{'}\left(x\right)}{f\left(x\right) + 1}dx = {∫}_{0}^{x}{e}^{x}dx$

${ln\left(f\left(x\right) + 1\right)}_{0}^{x}{= {e}^{x}}_{0}^{x}$

$ln\left(f\left(x\right) + 1\right) - ln\left(f\left(0\right) + 1\right) = {e}^{x} - 1$

$ln\left(\dfrac{f\left(x\right) + 1}{2}\right) = {e}^{x} - 1$ {as $f\left(0\right) = 1$}

$f\left(x\right) = 2{e}^{\left({e}^{x} - 1\right)} - 1$

questions.q: The value of ${∫}_{- \pi / 2}^{\pi / 2}\dfrac{\cos^{2}x}{1 + {3}^{x}}dx$ is:
questions.solution:
Given $I = {∫}_{- \pi / 2}^{\pi / 2}\dfrac{\cos^{2}x}{1 + {3}^{x}}dx . . . \left(i\right)$

Using ${∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right)dx,$ we get

$I = {∫}_{- \pi / 2}^{\pi / 2}\dfrac{\cos^{2}x}{1 + {3}^{- x}}dx = {∫}_{- \pi / 2}^{\pi / 2}\dfrac{{3}^{x}\cos^{2}x}{1 + {3}^{x}}dx . . . \left(ii\right)$

Adding $\left(i\right) \text{ and } \left(ii\right)$ we get,

$2I = {∫}_{- \pi / 2}^{\pi / 2}\dfrac{\left(1 + {3}^{x}\right)\cos^{2}x}{1 + {3}^{x}}dx$

$2I = {∫}_{- \pi / 2}^{\pi / 2}\cos^{2}xdx$

$2I = 2{∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\cos^{2}xdx$

$I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\cos^{2}xdx$

$I = \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\left(1 + cos2x\right)dx = \dfrac{1}{2}{\left[x + \dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right]}_{0}^{\pi / 2}$

$I = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

questions.q: The integral ${∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}\tan^{3}x \cdot \sin^{2}3x\left(2{sec}^{2}x \cdot \sin^{2}3x + 3tanx \cdot sin6x\right)dx$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Rearranging, we get,

${∫}_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}\left(\dfrac{\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\tan^{4}x\right)}{2} \cdot \sin^{4}3x + \tan^{4}x \cdot \dfrac{\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\sin^{4}3x\right)}{2}\right)dx$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}\left(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\tan^{4}x \cdot \sin^{4}3x\right)\right)dx$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}{\left[\tan^{4}x \cdot \sin^{4}3x\right]}_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{\left(\sqrt{3}\right)}^{4} \times 0 - {\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)}^{4} \times 1\right]$

$= - \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{9} = - \dfrac{1}{18}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\left\{x\right\}$ and $\left[x\right]$ denote the fractional part of $x$ and the greatest integer $\le x$ respectively of a real number $x$. if ${∫}_{0}^{n}\left\{x\right\}dx, {∫}_{0}^{n}\left[x\right]dx$ and $10\left({n}^{2} - n\right), ( n \in N, n > 1 )$ are three consecutive terms of a G.P. then $n$ is equal to__
questions.solution:
${∫}_{0}^{n}\left\{x\right\}dx = n{∫}_{0}^{1}xdx = n{\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right)}_{0}^{1} = \dfrac{n}{2}$
and ${∫}_{0}^{n}\left[x\right]dx = {∫}_{0}^{n}\left(x - \left\{x\right\}\right)dx = {\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right)}_{0}^{n} - {∫}_{0}^{n}\left\{x\right\}dx = \dfrac{{n}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{n}{2}$
Now, $\dfrac{n}{2}, \dfrac{{n}^{2} - n}{2}$ and $10\left({n}^{2} - n\right)$ are in Geometric progression

So,${\left(\dfrac{{n}^{2} - n}{2}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{n}{2} \cdot 10\left({n}^{2} - n\right)$
$⇒ \dfrac{{n}^{2} ( n - 1{)}^{2}}{4} = 5 . {n}^{2} ( n - 1 )$
$⇒ n - 1 = 20 ⇒ n = 21$\left(∵ n \ne 1\right)$

questions.explanation:

and ${∫}_{0}^{n}\left[x\right]dx = {∫}_{0}^{n}\left(x - \left\{x\right\}\right)dx = {\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right)}_{0}^{n} - {∫}_{0}^{n}\left\{x\right\}dx = \dfrac{{n}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{n}{2}$
Now, $\dfrac{n}{2}, \dfrac{{n}^{2} - n}{2}$ and $10\left({n}^{2} - n\right)$ are in Geometric progression

So,${\left(\dfrac{{n}^{2} - n}{2}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{n}{2} \cdot 10\left({n}^{2} - n\right)$
$⇒ \dfrac{{n}^{2} ( n - 1{)}^{2}}{4} = 5 . {n}^{2} ( n - 1 )$
$⇒ n - 1 = 20 ⇒ n = 21$\left(∵ n \ne 1\right)$

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = \left|x - 2\right|$ and $g\left(x\right) = f\left(f\left(x\right)\right), x \in \left[0, 4\right]$. Then ${∫}_{0}^{3}\left(g\left(x\right) - f\left(x\right)\right)dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$f\left(x\right) = \left|x - 2\right| = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}2 - x; x < 2 \\ x - 2; x \ge 2\end{array}\right$

$g\left(x\right) = f\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}2 - f\left(x\right); f\left(x\right) < 2 \\ f\left(x\right) - 2; f\left(x\right) \ge 2\end{array}\right$

$= \left\{\begin{array}{ll}2 - \left(2 - x\right); 2 - x < 2, x < 2 \\ \left(2 - x\right) - 2; 2 - x \ge 2, x < 2 \\ 2 - \left(x - 2\right); x - 2 < 2, x \ge 2 \\ \left(x - 2\right) - 2; x - 2 \ge 2, x \ge 2\end{array}\right$

$= \left\{\begin{array}{ll}2 - \left(2 - x\right); 0< x < 2 \\ \left(2 - x\right) - 2; x < 0 \\ 2 - \left(x - 2\right); 2 \le x < 4 \\ \left(x - 2\right) - 2; x \ge 4\end{array}\right$

$\mathop{∫}_{0}^{3}\left(g\left(x\right) - f\left(x\right)\right)dx = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{2}xdx + \mathop{∫}_{2}^{3}\left(4 - x\right)dx - \mathop{∫}_{0}^{3}\left|x - 2\right|dx$

$= {\left[\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right]}_{0}^{2} + {\left[4x - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right]}_{2}^{3} - {\left[2x - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right]}_{0}^{2} - {\left[\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} - 2x\right]}_{2}^{3}$

$= 1$.
questions.question: Let $f\left(x\right) = \left|x - 2\right|$ and $g\left(x\right) = f\left(f\left(x\right)\right), x \in \left[0, 4\right]$. Then ${∫}_{0}^{3}\left(g\left(x\right) - f\left(x\right)\right)dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation:
$f\left(x\right) = \left|x - 2\right| = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}2 - x; x < 2 \\ x - 2; x \ge 2\end{array}\right$

$g\left(x\right) = f\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}2 - f\left(x\right); f\left(x\right) < 2 \\ f\left(x\right) - 2; f\left(x\right) \ge 2\end{array}\right$

$= \left\{\begin{array}{ll}2 - \left(2 - x\right); 2 - x < 2, x < 2 \\ \left(2 - x\right) - 2; 2 - x \ge 2, x < 2 \\ 2 - \left(x - 2\right); x - 2 < 2, x \ge 2 \\ \left(x - 2\right) - 2; x - 2 \ge 2, x \ge 2\end{array}\right$

$= \left\{\begin{array}{ll}2 - \left(2 - x\right); 0< x < 2 \\ \left(2 - x\right) - 2; x < 0 \\ 2 - \left(x - 2\right); 2 \le x < 4 \\ \left(x - 2\right) - 2; x \ge 4\end{array}\right$

$\mathop{∫}_{0}^{3}\left(g\left(x\right) - f\left(x\right)\right)dx = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{2}xdx + \mathop{∫}_{2}^{3}\left(4 - x\right)dx - \mathop{∫}_{0}^{3}\left|x - 2\right|dx$

$= {\left[\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right]}_{0}^{2} + {\left[4x - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right]}_{2}^{3} - {\left[2x - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right]}_{0}^{2} - {\left[\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} - 2x\right]}_{2}^{3}$

$= 1$.

questions.q: If the value of the integral ${∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)}^{\dfrac{3}{2}}}dx$ is $\dfrac{k}{6}$, then $k$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{k}{6} = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)\dfrac{3}{2}}dx$

Let $x = sin\theta ⇒ dx = cos\thetad\theta$

$⇒ \dfrac{k}{6} = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}\dfrac{\sin^{2}\theta}{{\left(1 - \sin^{2}\theta\right)}^{\dfrac{3}{2}}}cos\thetad\theta ⇒ \dfrac{k}{6} = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}\dfrac{\sin^{2}\theta}{\left(\cos^{3}\theta\right)}cos\thetad\theta$

$⇒ \dfrac{k}{6} = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}\tan^{2}\thetad\theta = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}\left(se{c}^{2}\theta - 1\right)d\theta ⇒ \dfrac{k}{6} = {\left(tan\theta - \theta\right)}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{6}} = \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} - \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{2\sqrt{3} - \pi}{6}$

$⇒ k = 2\sqrt{3} - \pi$

questions.q: The integral ${∫}_{0}^{2}\left|\left|x - 1\right| - x\right|dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\begin{array}{ll}{∫}_{0}^{2}\left|\left|x - 1\right| - x\right|dx = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left|1 - x - x\right|dx + {∫}_{1}^{2}\left|x - 1 - x\right|dx\end{array}$

$= {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}\left(1 - 2x\right)dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}^{1}\left(2x - 1\right)dx + {∫}_{1}^{2}dx$

$= {\left(x - {x}^{2}\right)}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{2}} + {\left({x}^{2} - x\right)}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}^{1} + {\left(x\right)}_{1}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{4} - \left(0 - 0\right) + \left(1 - 1\right) - \left(\dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) + 2 - 1$

$= \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{4} + 1 = \dfrac{3}{2} = 1 . 5$

questions.q: The value of ${∫}_{0}^{2\pi}\dfrac{x\sin^{8} ⁡ x}{\sin^{8} ⁡ x + \cos^{8} ⁡ x}dx$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given, $I = {∫}_{0}^{2\pi}\dfrac{x\sin^{8} ⁡ x}{\sin^{8} ⁡ x + \cos^{8} ⁡ x}dx . . . \left(i\right)$

Use the property ${∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right)dx$ we get,

$I = {∫}_{0}^{2\pi}\dfrac{\left(2\pi - x\right)\sin^{8} ⁡ \left(2\pi - x\right)}{\sin^{8} ⁡ \left(2\pi - x\right) + \cos^{8} ⁡ \left(2\pi - x\right)}dx = {∫}_{0}^{2\pi}\dfrac{\left(2\pi - x\right)\sin^{8} ⁡ x}{\sin^{8} ⁡ x + \cos^{8} ⁡ x}dx . . . \left(ii\right)$

Adding equation $\left(i\right) \text{ and } \left(ii\right)$we get,

$2I = {∫}_{0}^{2\pi}\dfrac{2\pi\sin^{8} ⁡ x}{\sin^{8} ⁡ x + \cos^{8} ⁡ x}dx$

Use the property ${∫}_{0}^{2a}f\left(x\right)dx = 2{∫}_{0}^{a}f\left(2a - x\right)dx$ we get,

$I = 2{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{\pi\sin^{8} ⁡ x}{\sin^{8} ⁡ x + \cos^{8} ⁡ x}dx$

Use the property ${∫}_{0}^{2a}f\left(x\right)dx = 2{∫}_{0}^{a}f\left(2a - x\right)dx$we get,

$I = 4{∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\dfrac{\pi\sin^{8} ⁡ x}{\sin^{8} ⁡ x + \cos^{8} ⁡ x}dx . . . \left(iii\right)$

Use the property ${∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right)dx$ we get,

$I = 4{∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\dfrac{\pi\cos^{8} ⁡ x}{\sin^{8} ⁡ x + \cos^{8} ⁡ x}dx . . . \left(iv\right)\left(∵ sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right) = cosx\right)$

Adding the equation $\left(iii\right) \text{ and } \left(iv\right)$we get,

$2I = 4\pi{∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}1dx$

$⇒ I = 2\pi{\left[x\right]}_{0}^{\pi / 2} = {\pi}^{2}$

questions.q: A value of $\alpha$ such that $\mathop{∫}_{\alpha}^{\alpha + 1}\dfrac{dx}{( x + \alpha ) ( x + \alpha + 1 )} = lo{g}_{e}\left(\dfrac{9}{8}\right)$ is
questions.solution:
$I = \mathop{∫}_{\alpha}^{\alpha + 1}\dfrac{dx}{( x + \alpha ) ( x + \alpha + 1 )} =\mathop{∫}_{\alpha}^{\alpha + 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x + \alpha} – \dfrac{1}{x + \alpha + 1}\right)dx$
Using partial fractions
$= {\left[ln\left|x + \alpha\right| - ln\left|x + \alpha + 1\right|\right]}_{\alpha}^{\alpha + 1}$
$= {\left[ln\left|\dfrac{x + \alpha}{x + \alpha + 1}\right|\right]}_{\alpha}^{\alpha + 1}$
$= ln\left|\dfrac{2\alpha + 1}{2\alpha + 2}\right| - ln\left|\dfrac{2\alpha}{2\alpha + 1}\right|$
$= ln\left|\dfrac{{\left(2\alpha + 1\right)}^{2}}{{\left(2\alpha + 1\right)}^{2} - 1}\right| = ln ⁡ \dfrac{9}{8}$
$⇒ {( 2\alpha + 1 )}^{2} = 9$
$⇒ 2\alpha + 1 = \pm 3$
$⇒ \alpha = 1$ or $- 2$.

questions.q: If $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{cotx}{cotx + cosecx}dx = m ( \pi + n ),$ then $mn$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{cotx}{cotx + cosecx}dx$
$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{cosx}{cosx + 1}dx$
$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{cosx + 1 - 1}{cosx + 1}dx$
$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2\cos^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}}\right)dx$
$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}se{c}^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}\right)dx$
$⇒ I = {\left(x - tan\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}$
$⇒ I = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - 1\right) - \left(0 - 0\right)$
$⇒ I = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 1 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\pi - 2\right)$.

Now using given information $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{cotx}{cotx + cosecx}dx = m ( \pi + n ),$ clearly $m = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $n = - 2$.

$⇒ mn = - 1$

questions.q: The integral ${∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}sec\dfrac{2}{3}x \cdot cosec\dfrac{4}{3}xdx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $I = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}sec\dfrac{2}{3}x \cdot cosec\dfrac{4}{3}xdx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}\left(\dfrac{1}{cos\dfrac{2}{3}x \cdot sin\dfrac{4}{3}x}\right)dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}\left(\dfrac{\cos^{\dfrac{4}{3}}x}{\cos^{\dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{4}{3}}x \cdot \sin^{\dfrac{4}{3}}x}\right)dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}} \left(\dfrac{{sec}^{2}x}{\tan^{\dfrac{4}{3}}x}\right)dx$

Let $tanx = t, {sec}^{2}xdx = dt$ and at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}, t = tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ and at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}, t = tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \sqrt{3}$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}^{\sqrt{3}}\dfrac{dt}{t\dfrac{4}{3}}$

Using $∫ {x}^{n}dx = \dfrac{{x}^{n + 1}}{n + 1}$

$⇒ I = {\left[\dfrac{{t}^{- \dfrac{4}{3} + 1}}{- \dfrac{4}{3} + 1}\right]}_{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}^{\sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ I = {\left[- 3{t}^{- \dfrac{1}{3}}\right]}_{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}^{\sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ I = - 3\left\{{\left(\sqrt{3}\right)}^{- \dfrac{1}{3}} - {\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)}^{- \dfrac{1}{3}}\right\}$

$⇒ I = - 3\left\{{\left(3\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{- \dfrac{1}{3}} - {\left(\dfrac{1}{3\dfrac{1}{2}}\right)}^{- \dfrac{1}{3}}\right\}$

$= - 3\left(\dfrac{1}{3\dfrac{1}{6}} - 3\dfrac{1}{6}\right)$

$= \dfrac{- 3}{3\dfrac{1}{6}} + 3 \times 3\dfrac{1}{6}$

$= 3\dfrac{7}{6} - 3\dfrac{5}{6} .$

$⇒ 2I = - 2\pi$

$⇒ I = - \pi$

questions.q: The value of the integral ${∫}_{0}^{1}x{cot}^{- 1}\left(1 - {x}^{2} + {x}^{4}\right)dx$ is
questions.solution:
Given integral, $I = {∫}_{0}^{1}x{cot}^{- 1}\left(1 - {x}^{2} + {x}^{4}\right)dx$

Put ${x}^{2} = t, ⇒ 2xdx = dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}{cot}^{- 1}\left(1 - t + {t}^{2}\right)dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 - t + {t}^{2}}\right)dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{t - \left(t - 1\right)}{1 + t\left(t - 1\right)}\right)dt$

Using $\tan^{- 1}a - \tan^{- 1}b = \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{a - b}{1 + a \cdot b}\right),$ we get

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\tan^{- 1}t\right)dt - {∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1}\left(t - 1\right)dt\right]$

Using ${∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right)dx,$ we get

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\tan^{- 1}t\right)dt - {∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1}\left(\left(1 - t\right) - 1\right)dt\right]$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\tan^{- 1}t\right)dt - {∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1}\left(- t\right)dt\right]$

Now, using $\tan^{- 1}\left(- a\right) = - \tan^{- 1}a,$ we get

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\tan^{- 1}t\right)dt + {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\tan^{- 1}t\right)dt\right]$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[2{∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1}tdt\right]$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(1 ⋅ \tan^{- 1}t\right)dt$

Now applying the integration by parts i.e. ${∫}_{a}^{b}\left(u \cdot v\right)dx = u{∫}_{a}^{b}vdx - {∫}_{a}^{b}\left[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(u\right) ∫ vdx\right]dx + c$

$⇒ I = {\tan^{- 1}t ⋅ t |}_{0}^{1} - {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + {t}^{2}} ⋅ t\right)dt$

Put $1 + {t}^{2} = u, ⇒ 2tdt = du$

$⇒ I = \tan^{- 1}\left(1\right) ⋅ 1 - 0 - \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{1}^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{u}\right)du$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}{\log}_{2}\left(u\right){\left​\right|}_{1}^{2}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}{\log}_{e}2 .$

questions.q: If $f: R \to R$ is a differentiable function and $f\left(2\right) = 6,$ then $\lim_{x \to 2}{∫}_{6}^{f\left(x\right)}\dfrac{2tdt}{\left(x - 2\right)}$ is:
questions.solution:
The given limit can be written as

$l = \lim_{x \to 2}\dfrac{{∫}_{6}^{f\left(x\right)}2tdt}{\left(x - 2\right)}$

Applying L' Hospital’s rule i.e. if $l = \lim_{x \to a}\dfrac{g\left(x\right)}{h\left(x\right)}$ and $\lim_{x \to a}g\left(x\right) \to 0 \text{ and } \lim_{x \to a}h\left(x\right) \to 0,$ then $l = \lim_{x \to a}\dfrac{{g}^{'}\left(x\right)}{{h}^{'}\left(x\right)}$

$l = \lim_{x \to 2}\dfrac{\dfrac{d}{dx}{∫}_{6}^{f\left(x\right)}2tdt}{1}$

Now, applying Newton's Leibnitz rule i.e. $\dfrac{d}{dx}{∫}_{a}^{b}g\left(x\right)dx = g\left(b\right) \cdot {b}^{'} - g\left(a\right) \cdot {a}^{'},$ we get

$⇒ l = \lim_{x \to 2}\left(2f\left(x\right) \cdot {f}^{'}\left(x\right) - 0\right)$

$⇒ l = 2f\left(2\right) ⋅ {f}^{'}\left(2\right)$

Put the given value, to get

$⇒ l = 2 \times 6 \times {f}^{'}\left(2\right) = 12{f}^{'}\left(2\right) .$

questions.q: The value of $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\dfrac{\sin^{3}x}{sinx + cosx}dx$ is:
questions.solution:
$I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\sin^{3}x}{sinx + cosx}dx . . . \left(i\right)$

Using property of definite integration ${∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right)dx,$ we get

$I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\sin^{3}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right)}{sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right) + cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right)}dx$

Using $sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right) = cosx \text{ and } cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right) = sinx,$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\cos^{3}\left(x\right)}{cos\left(x\right) + sin\left(x\right)}dx . . . \left(ii\right)$

On adding the equation $\left(i\right) \text{ and } \left(ii\right)$

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\sin^{3}x + \cos^{3}x}{sinx + cosx}dx$

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\left(sinx + cosx\right)\left(\sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x - sinxcosx\right)}{sinx + cosx}dx$

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(\sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x - sinxcosx\right)dx$

Now, using $\sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x = 1 \text{ and } 2sinxcosx = sin2x,$ we get

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}sin2x\right)dx$

$⇒ 2I = {\left[x + \dfrac{cos2x}{4}\right]}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}$

$⇒ 2I = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} + \dfrac{cos2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}{4}\right) - \left(0 + \dfrac{cos2\left(0\right)}{4}\right)$

$⇒ 2I = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{1}{4}\right) - \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)$

$⇒ 2I = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{\pi - 1}{4} .$

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{x}g\left(t\right)dt,$ where $g$ is a non-zero even function. If $f\left(x + 5\right) = g\left(x\right),$ then $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{x}f ( t ) dt$ equals
questions.solution:
Given: $g\left(x\right)$ is an even function, then
$f\left(x\right) = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{x}g ( t ) dt$ will be an odd function,
$⇒ f\left(- x\right) = - f\left(x\right)$
Let $I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{x}f\left(t\right)dt$ put $t = z + 5$
$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{- 5}^{x - 5}f\left(z + 5\right)dz$
$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{- 5}^{x - 5}g ( z ) dz$\left(∵ f\left(x + 5\right) = g\left(x\right)\right)$
$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{- 5}^{x - 5}{f}^{'} ( z ) dz ( ∵ {f}^{'} ( x ) = g ( x ) )$
$⇒ I = f ( z ) {|}_{- 5}^{x - 5} = f ( x - 5 ) - f\left(- 5\right)$
$⇒ I = f ( 5 ) - f\left(5 + x\right)$ ( $f$ is an odd function and $g$ is given as an even function)
$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{5 + x}^{5}{f}^{'} ( t ) dt =\mathop{∫}_{5 + x}^{5}g ( t ) dt$

questions.q: If $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2 - xcosx}{2 + xcosx}$ and $g ( x ) = {\log}_{e} ⁡ x,$ then the value of the integral $\mathop{∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}g\left(f\left(x\right)\right)dx$ is
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2 - xcosx}{2 + xcosx},$g ( x ) = {\log}_{e} ⁡ x$

$⇒ g\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = lo{g}_{e}\left(\dfrac{2 - xcosx}{2 + xcosx}\right)$

$⇒ g\left(f\left(- x\right)\right) = ⁡ lo{g}_{e}\left(\dfrac{2 - ( - x ) cos ⁡ ( - x )}{2 + ( - x ) cos ⁡ ( - x )}\right)$

$⇒ g\left(f\left(- x\right)\right) = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{2 + xcosx}{2 - xcosx}\right)$

$⇒ g\left(f\left(- x\right)\right) = - log\left(\dfrac{2 - xcosx}{2 + xcosx}\right)$

$⇒ g\left(f\left(- x\right)\right) = – g ( f\left(x\right) )$

Hence, $g ( f\left(x\right) )$ is an odd function.

By using the property of definite integration, ${∫}_{- a}^{a}f\left(x\right) d x = \left\{\begin{cases}2{∫}_{0}^{a} & f\left(x\right)dx, f\left(- x\right) = f\left(x\right) \\ 0, & f\left(- x\right) = - f\left(x\right)\end{cases}\right$, we can write
$\mathop{∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}g ( f ( x ) ) dx =0 = {\log}_{e} ⁡ 1$

questions.q: The integral $\mathop{∫}_{1}^{e}\left\{{\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x} - {\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)}^{x}\right\}lo{g}_{e}xdx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let ${I}_{1} = {∫}_{1}^{e}{\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x}{{\log}_{e}x}_{} ⁡ dx$

Let ${\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{x} = t$

Taking natural logarithm on both sides, we get

$x\text\ln\dfrac{x}{e} = \text\lnt$

$⇒ x\left(\text\lnx - 1\right) = \text\lnt . . . . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

$x$ $t$
$1$ $1\left(ln1 - 1\right) = lnt ⇒ t = \dfrac{1}{e}$
$e$ $e\left(lne - 1\right) = lnt ⇒ t = 1$

Differentiating equation $\left(i\right)$ on both the sides, we get

$\text\lnx - 1 + x\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)dx = \dfrac{1}{t}dt$

$\text{⇒ln}xdx = \dfrac{1}{t}dt$

$∴ {I}_{1} = {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{e}}^{1}{t}^{2}\dfrac{1}{t}dt = {\left(\dfrac{{t}^{2}}{2}\right)}_{\dfrac{1}{e}}^{1} = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2{e}^{2}}$

and ${I}_{2} = {∫}_{1}^{e}{\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)}^{x}{\log}_{e}x ⁡ dx$

Let ${\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)}^{x} = t$

Taking natural logarithm on both sides, we get

$xln\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right) = lnt$

$⇒ x\left(1 - lnx\right) = lnt . . . . . . . . . \left(ii\right)$

$x$ $t$
$1$ $1\left(1 - ln1\right) = lnt ⇒ t = e$
$e$ $e\left(1 - lne\right) = lnt ⇒ t = 1$

Differentiating equation $\left(ii\right)$ both sides, we get

$⇒ \left[x\left(0 - \dfrac{1}{x}\right) + \left(1 - lnx\right) . 1\right]dx = \dfrac{dt}{t}$ (using product rule of differentiation)

$⇒ lnx = - \dfrac{dt}{t}$

$∴ {I}_{2} = {∫}_{e}^{1}t . \dfrac{- dt}{t} = {\left(- t\right)}_{e}^{1} = \left(- 1\right) - \left(- e\right) = e - 1$

Hence, required integral is ${I}_{1} - {I}_{2}$

$= \left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2{e}^{2}}\right) - \left(e - 1\right)$

$= \dfrac{3}{2} - e - \dfrac{1}{2{e}^{2}}$.

questions.solution:

$⇒ I = 4{∫}_{0}^{a}f\left(x\right)dx - I$

$⇒ 2I = 4{∫}_{0}^{a}f\left(x\right)dx$

$⇒ I = 2{∫}_{0}^{a}f\left(x\right)dx$

questions.q: The value of integral $\int_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{4}} \frac{x}{1+\sin x} d x$ is
questions.solution:
Let $I=\int_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{4}} \frac{x}{1+\sin x} d x$ also let $K=\frac{x}{1+\sin x}$
Multiplying numerator and denominator by $(1-\sin x)$, we get;
$
\begin{aligned}
K &=\frac{x(1-\sin x)}{1-(\sin x)^2}=\frac{x(1-\sin x)}{(\cos x)^2} \\
&=x(1-\sin x) \sec ^2 x \\
&=x \sec ^2 x-x \sin x \sec ^2 x=x \sec ^2 x-x \tan \\
x & \sec x
\end{aligned}
$
Now, $I=\int_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{4}} x \sec ^2 x d x-\int_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{4}} x \sec x \tan x d x$$
=\left[x \tan x-\int \frac{d x}{d x} \tan x d x\right]_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{4}}-\left[x \sec x-\int \frac{d x}{d x} \sec x d x\right]_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{4}}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
&=[x \tan x-\ln |\sec x|]_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{4}} \\
&-[x \sec x-\ln |\sec x+\tan x|]_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{4}}+c \\
&\Rightarrow I=\left\{\left[\frac{3 \pi}{4} \tan \frac{3 \pi}{4}-\ln \left|\frac{3 \pi}{4}\right|\right.\right. \\
&\left.-\left[\frac{3 \pi}{4} \sec \frac{3 \pi}{4}-\ln \left|\sec \frac{3 \pi}{4}+\tan \frac{3 \pi}{4}\right|\right]\right\} \\
&-\left\{\left[\frac{\pi}{4} \tan \frac{\pi}{4}-\ln \left|\frac{\pi}{4}\right|\right.\right. \\
&\left.-\left[\frac{\pi}{4} \sec \frac{\pi}{4}-\ln \left|\sec \frac{\pi}{4}+\tan \frac{\pi}{4}\right|\right]\right\} \\
&=\frac{\pi}{2}(\sqrt{2}+1)
\end{aligned}
$

questions.solution:
$I = \mathop{∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\sin^{4} ⁡ x\left(1 + ln ⁡ \left(\dfrac{2 + sin ⁡ x}{2 - sin ⁡ x}\right)\right)dx . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

$I = 2\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\sin^{4}xdx . . . . . . . . . . . . \left(i\right), \left(∵ \sin^{4}x\text{is an even function}\right)$

$\left(∵ \mathop{∫}_{- \dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left(\sin^{4}x\right)ln ⁡ \left(\dfrac{2 + sinx}{2 - sinx}\right)dx = 0, ∵ \left(\sin^{4}x\right)ln ⁡ \left(\dfrac{2 + sinx}{2 - sinx}\right)\text{is odd function}\right)$

Let $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\sin^{4}xdx = m$

$⇒ m = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\sin^{4}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right)dx = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\cos^{4}\left(x\right)dx$

Adding both, we get

$⇒ 2m = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\sin^{4}\left(x\right)dx + \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\cos^{4}\left(x\right)dx$

$⇒ 2m = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left\{\sin^{4}\left(x\right) + \cos^{4}\left(x\right)\right\}dx$

$⇒ 2m = {\left(\sin^{2}\left(x\right) + \cos^{2}\left(x\right)\right)}^{2} - 2\sin^{2}\left(x\right)\cos^{2}\left(x\right)$

$⇒ 2m = 1 - \dfrac{\sin^{2}\left(2x\right)}{2}$

$⇒ 2m = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left\{1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{1 - cos4x}{2}\right)\right\}dx = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\left\{\dfrac{3}{4} + \dfrac{cos4x}{4}\right\}dx$

$⇒ 2m = {\left[\dfrac{3x}{4} + \dfrac{sin4x}{16}\right]}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}} = \dfrac{3\pi}{8}$

$⇒ m = \dfrac{3\pi}{16}$

Substituting in equation $\left(i\right)$, we get

$I = 2m = \dfrac{3\pi}{8}$

questions.q: The integral $\mathop{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{12}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{8cos2x}{{\left(tanx + cotx\right)}^{3}}dx$ equals
questions.solution:
Given

$\mathop{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{12}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{8cos2x}{{\left(tanx + cotx\right)}^{3}}dx = \mathop{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{12}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{8cos2x}{{\left(\dfrac{sinx}{cosx} + \dfrac{cosx}{sinx}\right)}^{3}}dx$

$= \mathop{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{12}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{cos2x}{{\left(\dfrac{1}{sin2x}\right)}^{3}} = \mathop{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{12}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}cos2x \cdot sin2x \cdot \sin^{2}\left(2x\right)dx$

$= \dfrac{1}{4}\mathop{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{12}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}sin4x \cdot ( 1 - cos4x )dx$

$= \dfrac{1}{4}\mathop{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{12}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}sin4x - \dfrac{1}{8}\mathop{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{12}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}sin8x$

$= - \dfrac{1}{16}{\left[cos4x\right]}_{\dfrac{\pi}{12}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}} + \dfrac{1}{8 \times 8}{\left[cos8x\right]}_{\dfrac{\pi}{12}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}$

$= - \dfrac{1}{16}\left[- 1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right] + \dfrac{1}{64}\left[1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\right]$

$= \dfrac{15}{128}$.

questions.q: For $x \in R, x \ne 0,$ if $y\left(x\right)$ is a differentiable function such that $x\mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}y\left(t\right)dt = \left(x + 1\right)\mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}ty\left(t\right)dt,$ then $y\left(x\right)$ equals (where $C$ is a constant)
questions.solution:
$x\mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}y\left(t\right)dt = x\mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}ty\left(t\right)dt + \mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}ty\left(t\right)dt$

Differentiate w.r.t. $x$

$\mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}y ( t ) dt + xy ( x ) = \mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}ty ( t ) dt + x [ xy ( x ) ] + xy ( x )$

$\mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}y ( t ) dt = \mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}ty ( t ) dt + {x}^{2}y ( x )$

Differentiate again w.r.t. $x$

$y ( x ) = xy ( x ) + 2xy ( x ) + {x}^{2}{y}^{'} ( x )$

$\left(1 - 3x\right)y\left(x\right) = {x}^{2}{y}^{'}\left(x\right)$

$\dfrac{{y}^{'}\left(x\right)}{y\left(x\right)} = \dfrac{1 - 3x}{{x}^{2}}$

$\dfrac{1}{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1 - 3x}{{x}^{2}}$

Integrating on both sides

$⇒ lny = - \dfrac{1}{x} - 3lnx + C$

$⇒ ln ( y{x}^{3} ) = - \dfrac{1}{x} + C$

$⇒ y{x}^{3} = {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{x} + C}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{{e}^{- \dfrac{1}{x} + C}}{{x}^{3}}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{C}{{x}^{3}}{e}^{- \dfrac{1}{x}}$

questions.q: If $2\mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1}xdx = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}{cot}^{- 1}\left(1 - x + {x}^{2}\right)dx$, then $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1}\left(1 - x + {x}^{2}\right)dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
From the given equation

$2\mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1} ⁡ xdx = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \tan^{- 1} ⁡ \left(1 - x + {x}^{2}\right)\right)dx$

$⇒ 2\mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1} ⁡ xdx = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{\pi}{2}dx - \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1} ⁡ \left(1 - x + {x}^{2}\right)dx$
$⇒ \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1} ⁡ \left(1 - x + {x}^{2}\right)dx = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 2\mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1} ⁡ xdx \ldots \left(i\right)$
Let ${I}_{1} = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1} ⁡ xdx$

$= {\left[\left(\tan^{- 1} ⁡ x\right)x\right]}_{0}^{1} - \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{1 + {x}^{2}}xdx$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{x}{1 + {x}^{2}}dx$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{2x}{1 + {x}^{2}}dx$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}{\left[ln\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right)\right]}_{0}^{1}$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}ln ⁡ 2$

By equation $\left(i\right)$,

${∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1} ⁡ \left(1 - x + {x}^{2}\right)dx = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 2\left[\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}ln2\right] = ln ⁡ 2$

questions.q: Let $f: R \to R$ be a function such that $f\left(2 - x\right) = f\left(2 + x\right)$ and $f\left(4 - x\right) = f\left(4 + x\right)$, for all $x \in R$ and $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{2}f\left(x\right)dx = 5$. Then the value of $\mathop{∫}_{10}^{50}f\left(x\right)dx$ is
questions.solution:
$f\left(2 - x\right) = f\left(2 + x\right)$ and $f\left(4 - x\right) = f ( 4 + x )$

Then curve is symmetric about $x = 2$ and $x = 4$

$∴$ The curve is periodic with period $4$

Given $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{2}f\left(x\right)dx = 5$

$\mathop{∫}_{0}^{4}f\left(x\right)dx = 2\mathop{∫}_{0}^{2}f\left(x\right)dx = 10$

$\mathop{∫}_{10}^{50}f\left(x\right)dx = \mathop{∫}_{2\left(4\right) + 2}^{12\left(4\right) + 2}f\left(x\right)dx$

questions.explanation:
$f\left(2 - x\right) = f\left(2 + x\right)$ and $f\left(4 - x\right) = f ( 4 + x )$

Then curve is symmetric about $x = 2$ and $x = 4$

$∴$ The curve is periodic with period $4$

$\mathop{∫}_{0}^{4}f\left(x\right)dx = 2\mathop{∫}_{0}^{2}f\left(x\right)dx = 10$

questions.q: For $x > 0,$ let $f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{log ⁡ t}{1 + t}dt .$ Then $f\left(x\right) + f\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$f\left(x\right) = \mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{log ⁡ t}{1 + t}dt$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{log ⁡ z}{( 1 + z )}dz$
And $f\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) = \mathop{∫}_{1}^{\dfrac{1}{x}}\dfrac{log ⁡ t}{1 + t}dt$
Put $t = \dfrac{1}{z}$
$dt = - \dfrac{1}{{z}^{2}}dz$
$f\left(x\right) = \mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{log ⁡ z}{{z}^{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{z}\right)} ⋅ dz$
$f\left(x\right) = \mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{log ⁡ z}{z ( 1 + z )}dz$
$f\left(x\right) + f\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) = \mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}log ⁡ z\left[\dfrac{1}{1 + z} + \dfrac{1}{z ( 1 + z )}\right]dz$
$= \mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{1}{z}log ⁡ zdz$
Put $log ⁡ z = P$⇒ \dfrac{1}{z}dz = dP$
$\mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}P ⋅ dP = {\left(\dfrac{{P}^{2}}{2}\right)}_{1}^{x} = \dfrac{1}{2}{\left(\log^{2} ⁡ z\right)}_{1}^{x} = \dfrac{{\left(log ⁡ x\right)}^{2}}{2}$

questions.q: Let, the function $F$ be defined as $F\left(x\right) = {∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{{e}^{t}}{t}dt, x > 0,$ then the value of the integral ${∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{{e}^{t}}{t + a}dt,$ where $a > 0,$ is
questions.solution:
Given $F\left(x\right) = {∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{{e}^{t}}{t}dt$

Let, $I = {∫}_{1}^{x}\dfrac{{e}^{t}}{t + a}dt$

Let, $t + a = y$⇒ dt = dy$

Also, $t = 1 ⇒ y = 1 + a$ and $t = x ⇒ y = x + a$

$∴ I = {∫}_{1 + a}^{x + a}\dfrac{{e}^{y - a}}{y}dy$

$⇒ I = {e}^{- a}{∫}_{1 + a}^{x + a}\dfrac{{e}^{y}}{y}dy$

Using ${∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(t\right)dt,$ we get

$I = {e}^{- a}{∫}_{1 + a}^{x + a}\dfrac{{e}^{t}}{t}dt$

$⇒ I = {e}^{- a}\left[{∫}_{1}^{1 + a}\dfrac{{e}^{t}}{t}dt + {∫}_{1 + a}^{x + a}\dfrac{{e}^{t}}{t}dt - {∫}_{1}^{1 + a}\dfrac{{e}^{t}}{t}dt\right]$

Using ${∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)dx + {∫}_{b}^{c}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{a}^{c}f\left(x\right)dx, a < c < b,$

$⇒ I = {e}^{- a}\left[{∫}_{1}^{x + a}\dfrac{{e}^{t}}{t}dt - {∫}_{1}^{1 + a}\dfrac{{e}^{t}}{t}dt\right]$

Using, the given relation, we get

$I = {e}^{- a}\left[F\left(x + a\right) - F\left(1 + a\right)\right] .$

questions.q: The integral $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}\dfrac{ln\left(1 + 2x\right)}{1 + 4{x}^{2}}dx$ equals
questions.solution:
We have, $I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}\dfrac{ln\left(1 + 2x\right)}{1 + 4{x}^{2}}dx$

Let, $2x = tan\theta ⇒ dx = \dfrac{1}{2}se{c}^{2}\thetad\theta$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}} ln \left(1 + tan\theta\right)d\theta$
$= \dfrac{1}{2}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}} ln \left(1 + tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \theta\right)\right)d\theta$

$\left(∵ {∫}_{0}^{a}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{0}^{a}f\left(a - x\right)dx\right)= \dfrac{1}{2}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}} ln \left(1 + \dfrac{1 - tan\theta}{1 + tan\theta}\right)d\theta$

$⇒ 2I = \left(ln2\right)\dfrac{\pi}{4} - 2I$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\pi}{16}\left(ln2\right)$

questions.q: The integral $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\sqrt{1 + 4{\text\sin}^{2}\dfrac{x}{2} - 4\text\sin\dfrac{x}{2}}dx$ equals
questions.solution:
$\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\sqrt{1 + 4{\text\sin}^{2}\dfrac{x}{2} - 4\text\sin\dfrac{x}{2}}dx$

$= \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\sqrt{{\left(2\text\sin\dfrac{x}{2} - 1\right)}^{2}}dx$

$= \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left|2\text\sin\dfrac{x}{2} - 1\right|dx$

$= 2\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left|\text\sin\dfrac{x}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right|dx$

$= 2\left[\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi / 3}\left|\text\sin\dfrac{x}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right|dx + \mathop{∫}_{\pi / 3}^{\pi}\left|\text\sin\dfrac{x}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right|dx\right]$

$= 2\left[\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi / 3} - \left(\text\sin\dfrac{x}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)dx + \mathop{∫}_{\pi / 3}^{\pi}\left(\text\sin\dfrac{x}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)dx\right]$

$= 2\left[{\left[2\text\cos\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{x}{2}\right]}_{0}^{\pi / 3} + {\left[- 2\text\cos\dfrac{x}{2} - \dfrac{x}{2}\right]}_{\pi / 3}^{\pi}\right]$

$= 2 \left[\left[2 \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + \dfrac{\pi}{6} - 2\right] + \left[- \dfrac{\pi}{2} + 2 \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right]\right]$

$= 2 \left[\sqrt{3} + \dfrac{\pi}{6} - 2 - \dfrac{\pi}{2} + \sqrt{3} + \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right]$

$= 2 \left[2 \sqrt{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{6} - 2\right]$

$= 4 \sqrt{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{3} - 4$.

questions.q:
Statement - I : The value of the integral $\mathop{∫}_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}\dfrac{dx}{1 + \sqrt{tanx}}$ is equal to $\dfrac{\pi}{6} .$

Statement - II : $\mathop{∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)dx = \mathop{∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right)dx .$
options: Statement - $I$ is true; Statement - $II$ is false.
Statement - $I$ is false; Statement - $II$ is true.
Statement - $I$ true; Statement - $II$ is true; Statement - $II$ is a correct explanation for Statement - $I$.
Statement - $I$ is true; Statement - $II$ is true; Statement - $II$ is not a correct explanation for Statement - $I$.
questions.solution:
Statement $II$ is a standard property of definite integrals.

For statement $I$ : $I = \mathop{∫}_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}\dfrac{dx}{1 + \sqrt{tanx}} = \mathop{∫}_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}\dfrac{dx}{1 + \sqrt{cotx}}$

$I = \mathop{∫}_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}\dfrac{\sqrt{tanx}}{1 + \sqrt{tanx}}dx = \mathop{∫}_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}\dfrac{\sqrt\sinx}{\sqrt\cosx + \sqrt{sinx}}dx = \mathop{∫}_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}\dfrac{\sqrt\cosx}{\sqrt\cosx + \sqrt{sinx}}dx$

$2I = \mathop{∫}_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}dx$

$2I = \dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$I = \dfrac{\pi}{12}$

Hence, statement $I$ is false.
